STUDYQURAN:39:intro/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:intro/r11.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:39:intro/r11.claim: The death passage shows disbelievers’ desperate end; verse 53 then emphasizes that God’s mercy and forgiveness remain available even to those who squandered their souls.
STUDYQURAN:39:intro/r11.anchor: A passage on death emphasizes the desperate circumstances of those who disbelieve when they meet their final end

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p521/r9.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p521/r9.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p521/r9.claim: The following discussion places life and death entirely under God's authority.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p521/r9.anchor: It is explained that life and death is fully under God’s authority

IBNMUJAHID:v1p561/r6.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p561/r6.speaker: حمزة، الكسائي
IBNMUJAHID:v1p561/r6.claim: They read قضى with ḍamma on qāf, fatḥa on yāʾ, and الموت nominative; the other readers use fatḥa on qāf and accusative الموت.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p561/r6.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائى ﴿ قضى ﴾ بضم القاف وفتح الياء ﴿ الموت ﴾ رفعا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p206/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p206/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p206/r6.claim: The author identifies the souls God takes at death with spirits.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p206/r6.anchor: والأنفس هي الأرواح. وقيل: النفس غير الروح، قاله ابن عباس.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p206/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p206/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p206/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas is reported to distinguish soul from spirit: spirit governs life, while soul governs sensation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p206/r7.anchor: قاله ابن عباس. فالروح لها تدبير عالم الحياة، والنفس لها تدبير عالم الإحساس.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p206/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p206/r8.speaker: فرقة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p206/r8.claim: One group distinguishes the discriminating soul from the imaginative soul.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p206/r8.anchor: وفرقت فرقة بين نفس التمييز ونفس التخييل.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p206/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p206/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p206/r9.claim: Hadith and Arabic usage indicate that nafs and ruh are synonyms, and their departure from the body is death.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p206/r9.anchor: والذي يدل عليه الحديث واللغة أن النفس والروح مترادفان، وأن فراق ذلك من الجسد هو الموت.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p206/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p206/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p206/r10.claim: Taking souls means causing death; the verse also compares sleep to death because sleepers do not discern or act, as in 6:60.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p206/r10.anchor: ومعنى يتوفى النفس: يميتها، والتي: أي والأنفس التي لم تمت في منامها، أي يتوفاها حين تنام، تشبيها للنوام بالأموات. ومنه: وهو الذي يتوفاكم بالليل .

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p206/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p206/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p206/r11.claim: God retains the soul of one who has truly died and returns the sleeping soul to its body until its appointed death.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p206/r11.anchor: فيمسك من قضى عليه الموت الحقيقي، ولا يردها في وقتها حية ويرسل النائمة لجسدها إلى أجل ضربه لموتها.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p206/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p206/r12.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p206/r12.claim: An alternative reading of taking is that God fully receives souls of life and movement, while sleep takes only the discerning soul, not the life-soul.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p206/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p206/r13.speaker: الأكثرون
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p206/r13.claim: Most hold that the soul is taken while the spirit remains in the sleeping body, as breathing and turning show.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p206/r13.anchor: وكون النفس تقبض، والروح في الجسد حالة النوم، بدليل أنه يتقلب ويتنفس، هو قول الأكثرين.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p206/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p206/r14.speaker: ابن جبير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p206/r14.claim: The passage attributes to Ibn Jubayr and one report from Ibn Abbas a position in the debate over whether soul and spirit are distinct or one.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p206/r14.anchor: ودل على التغاير وكونها شيئا واحدا هو قول ابن جبير وأحد قولي ابن عباس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p206/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p206/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p206/r15.claim: Taking the dead and sleeping souls, retaining and returning them until a term, supplies signs of God's power and knowledge for reflective people.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p206/r15.anchor: إن في ذلك: أي في توفي الأنفس مائتة ونائمة، وإمساكها وإرسالها إلى أجل، لآيات: لعلامات دالة على قدرة الله وعلمه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p206/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p206/r16.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p206/r16.claim: The majority read قضى actively with الموت in the accusative; several named readers read it passively with الموت nominative.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p206/r16.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: قضى مبنيا للفاعل، الموت: نصبا وابن وثاب، والأعمش، وطلحة، وعيسى، وحمزة، والكسائي: مبنيا للمفعول الموت: رفعا.

MUQATIL:39:75/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:39:75/r3.speaker: أبو جبير
MUQATIL:39:75/r3.claim: Abu Jubayr says God takes the souls of the dead and returns the souls of the living until an appointed time, without taking them; this contains signs for those who reflect.
MUQATIL:39:75/r3.anchor:
عن أبى جبير، فى قوله تعالى:
الله يتوفى الأنفس حين موتها والتي لم تمت في منامها
[الزمر: 42] قال: تقبض أنفس الأموات وترسل أنفس الأحياء إلى أجل مسمى

SAMIN-DURR:39:42/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:42/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:39:42/r1.claim: والتي لم تمت coordinates with الأنفس: God takes souls at death and also the souls that have not died during sleep.
SAMIN-DURR:39:42/r1.anchor: والتي لم تمت }: عطف على الأنفس أي: يتوفى الأنفس حين تموت، ويتوفى أيضا الأنفس التي لم تمت في منامها.

SAMIN-DURR:39:42/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:42/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:39:42/r2.claim: في منامها is an adverbial attached to يتوفى.

SAMIN-DURR:39:42/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:42/r3.speaker: الأخوان
SAMIN-DURR:39:42/r3.claim: The two readers use passive قضي and put الموت in the nominative as نائب الفاعل.
SAMIN-DURR:39:42/r3.anchor: وقرأ الأخوان " قضي " مبنيا للمفعول، " الموت " رفعا لقيامه مقام الفاعل.

ZAJJAJ:v4p356/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p356/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p356/r5.claim: At death, God takes the soul by which a person lives, moves, and breathes; when asleep, He takes the discerning soul rather than the life-soul, since sleepers continue to breathe.
ZAJJAJ:v4p356/r5.anchor: أي ويتوفى الأنفس التي لم تمت في منامها، فالميتة المتوفاة

ZAJJAJ:v4p356/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p356/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p356/r6.claim: The soul taken during sleep is the soul of discernment, not the life-soul; if the latter departed, breathing would stop.
ZAJJAJ:v4p356/r6.anchor: لا نفس الحياة، لأن نفس الحياة إذا زالت زال معها النفس

ASAD-NOTES:39:42#n44/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:39:42#n44/r1.speaker: Razi
ASAD-NOTES:39:42#n44/r1.claim: Razi allegorically compares guidance to life and straying to death; temporary straying is like deathlike sleep followed by awakening.
ASAD-NOTES:39:42#n44/r1.anchor: According to Razi, this passage connects allegorically with the preceding - the light of guidance being likened to life

ASAD-NOTES:39:42#n44/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:39:42#n44/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:39:42#n44/r2.claim: Beyond the allegory, the verse affirms God's might and exclusive power to create and withdraw life.
ASAD-NOTES:39:42#n44/r2.anchor: of God's almightiness, and especially of His exclusive power to create and to withdraw life.

ASAD-NOTES:39:42#n44/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:39:42#n44/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:39:42#n44/r3.claim: Yatawaffa literally means taking something away fully; tropically it means causing death, dying, or death because vital impulses are wholly withdrawn.
ASAD-NOTES:39:42#n44/r3.anchor: the operative verb yatawaffa; it primarily denotes "He takes [something] away in full"; and because death is characterized

ASAD-NOTES:39:42#n44/r4.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:39:42#n44/r4.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:39:42#n44/r4.claim: Sleep is traditionally likened to death because consciousness is absent in both, temporarily and partially in sleep, permanently in death.
ASAD-NOTES:39:42#n44/r4.anchor: The traditional likening of sleep to death is due to the fact that in both cases the body appears to be devoid of consciousness

ASAD-NOTES:39:42#n44/r5.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:39:42#n44/r5.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:39:42#n44/r5.claim: Asad rejects translating anfus as souls here: the soul survives bodily death, so anfus means human beings.
ASAD-NOTES:39:42#n44/r5.anchor: The popular translation of anfus - p1. of nafs - as "souls" is certainly inappropriate in the above context

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p135/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p135/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p135/r1.claim: Bint al-Shatiʾ criticizes traditional accounts of rhetorical inimitability as rigid templates and inflated phrases; even al-Khattabi offered nothing convincing or substantial for modern Arabic readers.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p135/r1.anchor: يدور في هذا النطاق من القوالب التقليدية الصماء والعبارات المضخمة التي لم يجد فيها مثل الخطابي

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p97/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p97/r1.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p97/r1.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read قضي عليها الموت as passive, with ḍamma on qāf and nominative الموت.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p97/r1.anchor: قال: قرأ حمزة والكسائي: قضي عليها الموت [الزمر/ 42] بضم القاف والياء مفتوحة والموت رفع

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p97/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p97/r2.speaker: الباقون
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p97/r2.claim: The other readers read active قضى with الموت accusative.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p97/r2.anchor: وقرأ الباقون: قضى بفتح القاف، الموت نصبا

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p97/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p97/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p97/r3.claim: The active reading is clearer because ويرسل الأخرى is active too; the passive has the same meaning but is less evident syntactically.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p97/r3.anchor: حجة بناء الفعل للفاعل قوله: ويرسل الأخرى [الزمر/ 42] فكما أن هذا الفعل مبني للفاعل

QIRAAT-ER:39:42:15#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:39:42:15#1/r1.speaker: Pss
QIRAAT-ER:39:42:15#1/r1.claim: The passive reading makes death the nominative subject of the decreed predicate, shifting from Allah decreeing death to death being decreed upon the soul.
QIRAAT-ER:39:42:15#1/r1.anchor: Pss, mutawatir: Canonical passive reading makes death nominative subject of the decreed predicate

ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r1.claim: God takes souls away from bodies by ending their governing relation to them.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r1.anchor: أي يقبضها عن الأبدان بأن يقطع تعلقها تعلق التصرف فيها عنها

ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r2.claim: At death God takes the soul at the time of death.

ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r3.claim: The clause about those who have not died is coordinated as a second object of yatawaffā; manāmihā can be a temporal noun or a gerund noun, meaning God takes them during sleep.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r3.anchor: متعلق بيتوفى أي يتوفاها في وقت نومها على أن مناما اسم زمان وجوز فيه كونه مصدرا ميميا

ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r4.claim: Both death and sleep involve taking souls from bodies and ending their governing relation, but death severs it inwardly and outwardly, while sleep severs it outwardly only.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r4.anchor: إلا أن توفيها حين الموت لتعلقها بها تعلق التصرف ظاهرا وباطنا وتوفيها في وقت النوم قطع لذلك ظاهر فقط

ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r5.claim: One explanation says “at death” because death is the same at its onset and later, while the taking in sleep varies in strength over the course of sleep.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r5.anchor: لكونه شيئا واحدا في أول زمان الموت وبعد مضي أيام منه قيل : ( حين موتها )

ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r6.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r6.claim: Some call the attribution of death and sleep to souls a metaphorical attribution, since these are states of their bodies.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r6.anchor: وإسناد الموت والنوم إلى الأنفس قيل : مجاز عقلي لأنهما حالا أبدانها لا حالاها

ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r7.speaker: الطبرسي
ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r7.claim: Al-Ṭabrisī treats the wording as ellipsis of a genitive, supplying “bodies.”
ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r7.anchor: وزعم الطبرسي أن الكلام على حذف مضاف أعني الأبدان

ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī takes “souls” to mean the whole person and explains death-taking as the complete loss of bodily health, life, sensation, and perception.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r8.anchor: وجعل الزمخشري الأنفس عبارة عن الجملة دون ما يقابل الأبدان وحمل توفيها على إماتتها

ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r9.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī takes sleepers as metaphorically dead: during sleep they lose discernment and action as the dead do, citing the verse about God taking people at night.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r9.anchor: وجعل الزمخشري الأنفس عبارة عن الجملة دون ما يقابل الأبدان وحمل توفيها على إماتتها

ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r10.claim: Putting God's name first and making it the subject of yatawaffā gives exclusivity, emphasis, or both; contextual focus favors exclusivity, since God alone truly takes souls.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r10.anchor: للحصر أو للتقوى أو لهما واعتبار الحصر أوفق بالمقام

ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r11.claim: God retains souls whose death He decreed eternally, does not return them to their bodies, and keeps them as they are; “retains” parallels “takes.”
ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r11.anchor: ولا يردها إلى أبدانها بل يبقيها على ما كانت عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r12.speaker: حمزة
ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r12.claim: Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, ʿĪsā, Ṭalḥa, al-Aʿmash, and Ibn Waththāb read the verb passively and make “death” nominative.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r12.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي وعيسى وطلحة والأعمش وابن وثاب ( قضى ) على البناء للمفعول ورفع ( الموت )

ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r13.claim: God sends the other souls, those of sleepers, back to their bodies, restoring their governing relation inwardly and outwardly; “sends” balances “retains.”
ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r13.anchor: وهي النائمة إلى أبدانها فتكون كما كانت حال اليقظة

ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r14.claim: The appointed limit is the time fixed for actual death and applies to the general class of sending after retention, rather than one instantaneous sending; this avoids implying no sleep after the first awakening.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r14.anchor: هو الوقت المضروب للموت حقيقة وهو غاية لجنس الإرسال الواقع بعد الإمساك لا لفرد منه آني

ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r15.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r15.claim: Another reading takes “sends” to include protection: God preserves the other soul from actual death until its appointed time.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r15.anchor: وقيل : ( يرسل ) مضمن معنى الحفظ والمراد يرسل الأخرى حافظا إياها عن الموت الحقيقي إلى أجل مسمى

ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r16.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r16.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās distinguishes soul and spirit: the soul gives reason and discernment, the spirit life and motion; both are taken at death, while only the soul is taken in sleep. Some attribute this distinction to most scholars.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r16.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس أن في ابن آدم نفسا وروحا بينهما مثل شعاع الشمس فالنفس هي التي بها العقل والتمييز والروح هي التي بها النفس والتحرك

ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r17.speaker: بعض الحكماء المتألهين
ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r17.claim: A theosophical sage describes a hierarchy: subtle vapor in the conical heart serves as a throne and instrument for the animal spirit, which in turn mirrors and mediates the rational or divine soul's governance of the body.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r17.anchor: قال بعض الحكماء المتألهين : إن القلب الصنوبري فيه بخار لطيف هو عرش للروح الحيوانية

ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r18.speaker: ابن جبير
ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r18.claim: Others deny a distinction between soul and spirit; this is attributed to Ibn Jubayr and one of Ibn ʿAbbās's two reported positions.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r18.anchor: وإلى عدم التغاير ذهب جماعة وهو قول ابن جبير واحد قولين لابن عباس

ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r19.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r19.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī argues the correct view is the whole-person account, since the pronoun returns to souls and the predicates death and sleep apply to the whole person rather than a soul apart from the body.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r19.anchor: وادعى أن الصحيح ما ذكره دون هذا المروي بدليل موتها ومنامها والضمير للأنفس وما أريد منها متصف بالموت والنوم

ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r20.speaker: الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r20.claim: Al-Kashf argues against distinguishing the two souls and favors the familiar sense of taking in full, then death, since full removal is present in death; al-Ālūsī questions this reasoning and cites sound reports that the taken are souls corresponding to bodies, not whole persons.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r20.anchor: ولأن الفرق بين النفسين رأى أن يدفعه البرهان وإيقاع الإستيفاء أيضا لابد له من تأويل أيضا فلا ينبغي أن يعدل عن المشهور

ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r21.speaker: أبو هريرة
ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r21.claim: In a report in the two Ṣaḥīḥ collections, the Prophet instructs sleepers to shake out their bedding and pray: if God retains my soul, have mercy on it; if He sends it, protect it as You protect Your righteous servants.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r21.anchor: أخرج الشيخان في صحيحيهما عن أبي هريرة قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r22.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r22.speaker: أبو قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r22.claim: The Prophet told Abū Qatāda's party on the night at al-Wādī that God took their spirits when He wished and returned them when He wished; the report is recorded by Aḥmad, al-Bukhārī, Abū Dāwūd, al-Nasāʾī, and Ibn Abī Shayba.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r22.anchor: وأخرج أحمد والبخاري وأبو داود والنسائي وابن أبي شيبة عن أبي قتادة أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لهم ليلة الوادي

ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r23.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r23.speaker: أنس بن مالك
ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r23.claim: Anas reports that, after he and the travelers slept and awoke in sunlight, the Prophet said souls are entrusted in servants' bodies and God takes or sends them whenever He wills. No grading is stated.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p7#3/r23.anchor: وأخرج ابن مردويه عن أنس بن مالك قال : كنت مع النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم في سفر

ALUSI-FULL:v24p8/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p8/r1.speaker: علي
ALUSI-FULL:v24p8/r1.claim: Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh transmit through Sulaym b. Amir that Umar asked why some dreams prove true; Ali answered that all souls are taken, and visions seen while in heaven are true.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p8/r1.anchor: فقال علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه

ALUSI-FULL:v24p8/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p8/r2.speaker: علي
ALUSI-FULL:v24p8/r2.claim: In Ali's account, souls released to their bodies encounter devils in the air, who mix falsehood into what they saw, making those dreams false.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p8/r2.anchor: إذا أرسلت إلى أجسادها تلقتها الشياطين في الهواء فكذبتها وأخبرتها بالأباطيل

ALUSI-FULL:v24p8/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p8/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p8/r3.claim: The report's apparent picture of the sleeping soul held in heaven until release needs interpretation if the soul is immaterial; this is not required by the alternative view of the soul.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p8/r3.anchor: وظاهر هذا الأثر أن النفس النائمة المقبوضة تكون في السماء حتى ترسل ومثل ذلك مما يجب تأويله على القول بتجرد النفس

ALUSI-FULL:v24p8/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p8/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p8/r4.claim: Al-Alusi describes the noble, celestial soul as descending to govern its bodily home, then using sleep as an opportunity to turn toward the world of light and receive some of its effects.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p8/r4.anchor: إن النفس شريفة علوية هبطت من المحل الأرفع وأرسلت من حمة ممنع وشغلت بتدبير منزلها

ALUSI-FULL:v24p8/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p8/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p8/r5.claim: A soul receiving from the perfected world of light sees true dreams; one turning back toward its worldly governance, amid delusions, sees false dreams, though individuals differ in readiness and insight.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p8/r5.anchor: فمتى رأت وهي تلك الحال مستفيضة من ذلك العالم الموصوف بالكمال رؤيا كانت صادقة

ALUSI-FULL:v24p9/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p9/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p9/r1.claim: The demonstrative refers to the described taking, retaining, and releasing of souls; its distance-form reflects the starting point, the fact that it was just mentioned, or its exalted rank.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p9/r1.anchor: الإشارة إلى ما ذكر من التوفي والإمساك والإرسال والإفراد لتأويله بالمذكور أو نحوه وصيغة البعيد

ALUSI-FULL:v24p9/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p9/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p9/r2.claim: The nunation of signs conveys abundance and greatness: the account supplies many magnificent proofs of God's power, wisdom, and encompassing mercy.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p9/r2.anchor: للتكثير والتعظيم أي إن فيما ذكر الآيات كثيرة عظيمة

ALUSI-FULL:v24p9/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p9/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p9/r3.claim: Reflectors consider how souls attach to bodies and are wholly taken at death, remaining without perishing until resurrection, or withdrawn only from outward bodily life in sleep and sent back repeatedly until their appointed terms.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p9/r3.anchor: في كيفية تعلق الأنفس بالأبدان وتوفيها عنها تارة بالكلية عند الموت وإمساكها باقية لا تفنى بفنائها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p121#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p121#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p121#2/r4.claim: Anfus means spirits; God takes them when provision is exhausted and lifespan ends; here death means bodily death.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p121#2/r4.anchor: فيقبضها عند فناء أكلها وانقضاء أجلها، وقوله: {حين موتها} يريد موت أجسادها.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p121#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p121#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p121#2/r5.claim: God takes souls of those not dead during sleep; this is the soul of intellect and discernment, distinct from the life-soul that leaves at death.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p121#2/r5.anchor: يريد يتوفى الأنفس التي لم تمت، {في منامها} والتي تتوفى عند النوم هي النفس التي يكون بها العقل والتمييز،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p121#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p121#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p121#2/r6.claim: The soul whose death God has decreed is held and not returned to the body.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p121#2/r6.anchor: قضى عليها الموت} فلا يردها إلى الجسد.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p121#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p121#2/r7.speaker: حمزة والكسائي والآخرون
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p121#2/r7.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read the verb passively and al-mawt nominative; others read actively with al-mawt accusative.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p121#2/r7.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي: "قضي" بضم القاف وكسر الضاد وفتح الياء، "الموت" رفع على ما لم يسم فاعله،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p121#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p121#2/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p121#2/r8.claim: God returns the soul not decreed to die to its body until the appointed time of death.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p121#2/r8.anchor: ويرد الأخرى وهي التي لم يقض عليها الموت إلى الجسد، {إلى أجل مسمى} إلى أن يأتي وقت موته.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p121#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p121#2/r9.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p121#2/r9.claim: One account distinguishes nafs and rūḥ: at sleep the nafs leaves while the rūḥ remains.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p121#2/r9.anchor: ويقال: للإنسان نفس وروح، فعند النوم تخرج النفس وتبقى الروح.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p121#2/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p121#2/r10.speaker: علي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p121#2/r10.claim: ʿAlī says the rūḥ exits during sleep but its ray remains, allowing dreams; it returns when one wakes faster than a moment.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p121#2/r10.anchor: وعن علي قال: تخرج الروح عند النوم ويبقى شعاعه في الجسد، فبذلك يرى الرؤيا،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p121#2/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p121#2/r11.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p121#2/r11.claim: Another account says living and dead spirits meet and recognize each other in dreams; God keeps dead spirits and returns the living to their bodies until life's end.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p121#2/r11.anchor: ويقال: إن أرواح الأحياء والأموات تلتقي في المنام فتتعارف ما شاء الله،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p121#2/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p121#2/r12.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p121#2/r12.claim: The Prophet's bedtime supplication asks for mercy if God holds one's soul and protection if He returns it; he also advises shaking out bedding with a garment's inner edge.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p121#2/r12.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "إذا أوى أحدكم إلى فراشه فلينفض فراشه بداخلة إزاره

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p122/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p122/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p122/r1.claim: Taking and sending souls are signs of God's power, as He does not err in holding some and sending others.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p122/r1.anchor: لدلالات على قدرته حيث لم يغلط في إمساك ما يمسك من الأرواح، وإرسال ما يرسل منها.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p122/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p122/r2.speaker: مقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p122/r2.claim: Muqātil says the sleep-time taking and return of a soul signals resurrection for people who reflect.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p122/r2.anchor: قال مقاتل: لعلامات لقوم يتفكرون في أمر البعث، يعني: إن توفي نفس النائم وإرسالها بعد التوفي دليل على البعث.

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:41-42/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:41-42/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:41-42/r5.claim: God takes souls by cutting their connection to and control of bodies, wholly inwardly and outwardly in death, but only outwardly during sleep.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:41-42/r5.anchor: بأن يقطع تعلقها عنها وتصرفها فيها

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:41-42/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:41-42/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:41-42/r6.claim: God keeps the soul destined for death and does not return it to its body.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:41-42/r6.anchor: فيمسك التي قضى عليها الموت } ولا يردها إلى البدن،

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:41-42/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:41-42/r7.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:41-42/r7.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read قُضِيَ passively and al-mawt in the nominative.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:41-42/r7.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي قضي بضم القاف وكسر الضاد والموت بالرفع

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:41-42/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:41-42/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:41-42/r8.claim: The sleeping soul returns to its body on waking, until its appointed death.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:41-42/r8.anchor: أي النائمة إلى بدنها عند اليقظة

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:41-42/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:41-42/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:41-42/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the nafs is for reason and discernment and rūḥ for life, like sun rays in relation; both are taken at death, only the nafs in sleep, close to Bayḍāwī’s account.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:41-42/r9.anchor: وما روي عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما: أن في ابن آدم نفسا وروحا

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:41-42/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:41-42/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:41-42/r10.claim: Soul-taking, retention, and return show God’s power, wisdom, and mercy; reflection considers body relation, persistence, happiness or misery, and return until death.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:41-42/r10.anchor: دالة على كمال قدرته وحكمته وشمول رحمته

BIQAI-FULL:v6p453/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p453/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p453/r1.claim: A deputy could not preserve people in guidance while absent, asleep, or dead; only the ever-present God can guard them from error, consoling the Prophet.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p453/r1.anchor: وكان حفظهم على الهدى وعن الضلال لا يكون عليه إلا لحاضر لا يغيب ولا يعتريه نوم ولا يطرقه موت

BIQAI-FULL:v6p453/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p453/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p453/r2.claim: The passage compares guidance with life and wakefulness, and misguidance with death and sleep; only God can bring about either pair.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p453/r2.anchor: من تشبيه الهداية بالحياة واليقظة والضلال بالموت والنوم

BIQAI-FULL:v6p453/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p453/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p453/r3.claim: Grasping this subtlety reveals God's power and makes afflictions easier to bear; the verse consoles the Prophet.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p453/r3.anchor: فمن عرف هذه الدقيقة عرف سر الله في القدرة , ومن عرف السر فيه هانت عليه المصائب

BIQAI-FULL:v6p453/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p453/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p453/r4.claim: The passage names God and attributes taking souls to Him because no one else can serve as guardian or deputy in this matter.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p453/r4.anchor: وأسند التوفي إليه سبحانه لأنه في بيان أنه لا يصلح للوكالة غيره أصلا

BIQAI-FULL:v6p453/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p453/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p453/r5.claim: The plural of paucity is used for the many souls to suggest that, despite their number, they are as one soul; the noun is not singularized lest unity be taken literally.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p453/r5.anchor: وعبر عن جمع الكثرة بجمع القلة إشارة إلى أنها وإن تجاوزت الحصر فهي كنفس واحدة , ولعله لم يوحده

BIQAI-FULL:v6p453/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p453/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p453/r6.claim: At death, souls are prevented from acting through their bodies in worldly life and are enclosed in death.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p453/r6.anchor: أي منعها من التصرف في أجسادها في هذه الحياة الدنيا كائنة في مماتها محبوسة فيه مظروفة له

BIQAI-FULL:v6p453/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p453/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p453/r7.claim: God also takes souls whose terms have not expired when they sleep, withholding sensory perception and bodily control for the duration of sleep.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p453/r7.anchor: بمنعها من التصرف بالحس والإدراك ما دام النوم موجودا مظروفة له لا شيء منها في الجسد

BIQAI-FULL:v6p453/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p453/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p453/r8.claim: Death and sleep share the loss of perception, awareness, and action in the body.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p453/r8.anchor: فالجانع بينهما عدم الإدراك والشعور والتصرف

BIQAI-FULL:v6p453/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p453/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p453/r9.claim: The paired wording presents death and sleep as distinct signs; saying “by its death and by its sleep” would not make that distinction clear.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p453/r9.anchor: ولو قيل : بموتها وبمنامها , لم يفد أن كلص من الموت والوفاة آية مغايرة للآخرى

BIQAI-FULL:v6p453/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p453/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p453/r10.claim: Because sleep ends and is paired with death, the passage indicates that death also ends: the same agent brings about both states.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p453/r10.anchor: ولما كان النوم منقضيا , دلنا بقرانه بالموت على أن الموت أيضا منقض , ولا بد لأن الفاعل لكل منهما واحد

BIQAI-FULL:v6p453/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p453/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p453/r11.claim: Here qaḍā means that God has concluded, decreed, and decisively settled the soul's death.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p453/r11.anchor: أي ختم وحكم وبت بتا مقدرا مفروغا منه

BIQAI-FULL:v6p453/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p453/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p453/r12.claim: The passive reading of “was decreed upon it” further clarifies the settled meaning and its ease.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p453/r12.anchor: وقراءة البناء للمفعول موضحة لهذا المعنى بزيادة اليسر والسهولة

BIQAI-FULL:v6p453/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p453/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p453/r13.claim: God keeps the dead soul with Him; while death surrounds it, it cannot direct its body, just as a sleeper cannot while sleep surrounds them.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p453/r13.anchor: لا تقدر على تصريف جسدها ما دام الموت محيطا بها كما أن النائمة كذلك ما دام النوم محيطا بها

BIQAI-FULL:v6p453/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p453/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p453/r14.claim: The soul whose death is postponed is held in sleep only until God wakes it and restores bodily control; this is the sending of the sleeper's soul.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p453/r14.anchor: أي التي أخر موتها , وجعلها مظروفة للمنام لأنها لم ينقض أجلها الذي ضربه لها بأن ينفى بالمنام فيوقظها لتصريف أبدانها

BIQAI-FULL:v6p453/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p453/r15.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p453/r15.claim: The dead soul remains until resurrection and the sleeping soul until death; only God knows the term, when He raises the dead and causes the sleeper to die.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p453/r15.anchor: لبعث الميتة ولموت النائمة , لا يعلمه غيره , فإذا جاء ذلك الأجل أمات النائمة وبعث الميتة

BIQAI-FULL:v6p453/r16.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p453/r16.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p453/r16.claim: The soul that sleeps is the same soul that dies: it is the spirit.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p453/r16.anchor: وقد ظهر من التقدير الذي هدى إليه قطعا السياق أن النفس التي تنام هي التي تموت وهي الروح

BIQAI-FULL:v6p454/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p454/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p454/r1.claim: Sleep is partial separation of the soul from the body and death a complete one; only God can create and alternate these states, so ending the lesser death proves His power to end the greater.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p454/r1.anchor: فالموت والنوم من جنس واحد إلا أن الموت انقطاع تام , والنوم انقطاع ناقص , فلا يقدر على إيجاد شيء واحد على نوعين

BIQAI-FULL:v6p454/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p454/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p454/r2.claim: The one who sets a limit to sleep's minor death can also end death itself at its appointed boundary.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p454/r2.anchor: وكلما قدر على إنهاء الموتة الصغرى بحد جعله لها فهو قادر على إنهاء الكبرى بمثل ذلك

BIQAI-FULL:v6p454/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p454/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p454/r3.claim: The proof of God's unique power leads to a rebuke of those who take intercessors besides Him: no one approaches His power or rank, much less equals Him.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p454/r3.anchor: ولا يكون شيء إلا بإذنه , ولا يقرب أحد من القدرة على شيء من فعله , فكيف بالقرب من رتبته فضلا عن مماثلته

BIQAI-FULL:v6p454/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p454/r9.speaker: ابن الصلاح
BIQAI-FULL:v6p454/r9.claim: Ibn al-Ṣalāḥ says that identifying the sleeping soul with the soul that dies is closest to the apparent meaning of Scripture and Sunna.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p454/r9.anchor: قال ابن الصلاح في فتاويه : وهو الأشبه بظاهر الكتاب والسنة - انتهى .

BIQAI-FULL:v6p454/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p454/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
BIQAI-FULL:v6p454/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that living and dead souls meet and converse; God retains the dead souls and returns the living souls to their bodies. Al-Haythamī says its transmitters are narrators of the Ṣaḥīḥ.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p454/r10.anchor: روى الطبراني في الأوسط - قال الهيثمي : ورجاله رجال الصحيح - عن ابن عباس رضي الله الله عنهما قال : تلتقي أرواح الأحياء والأموات

BIQAI-FULL:v6p454/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p454/r11.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v6p454/r11.claim: The Prophet taught a bedtime supplication asking God for mercy if He retains one's soul and protection if He sends it back.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p454/r11.anchor: وروى البخاري عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال ( إذا أوى أحدكم إلى فراشه فليقل )

DURR-FULL:v7p231/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p231/r1.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
DURR-FULL:v7p231/r1.claim: Ali explains to ʿUmar that God takes all souls; visions seen while souls are with Him in heaven are true, while devils meet souls returning to their bodies and falsify what they see.
DURR-FULL:v7p231/r1.anchor: أن عمر بن الخطاب قال: العجب من رؤيا الرجل أنه يبيت فيرى الشيء لم يخطر له على باله

DURR-FULL:v7p231/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p231/r2.speaker: أبو أيوب
DURR-FULL:v7p231/r2.claim: Abu Ayyub reports the Prophet’s bedtime prayer asking God, who takes souls in sleep and death, to forgive him if He takes him or protect him if He defers him.
DURR-FULL:v7p231/r2.anchor: عن أبي أيوب أنه سمع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حين كان نازلا عليه في بيته

DURR-FULL:v7p231/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p231/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v7p231/r3.claim: The Prophet advised shaking out one’s bed with the inner hem before lying down, then asking God to show mercy if He holds one’s soul or protect it if He releases it.
DURR-FULL:v7p231/r3.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: إذا أوى أحدكم إلى فراشه

DURR-FULL:v7p231/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p231/r4.speaker: أبو جحيفة
DURR-FULL:v7p231/r4.claim: Abu Juhayfa recounts that after the travelers slept through sunrise, the Prophet said they had been dead and God had returned their souls.
DURR-FULL:v7p231/r4.anchor: عن أبي جحيفة رضي الله عنه قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في سفره الذي ناموا فيه

DURR-FULL:v7p231/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p231/r5.speaker: أبو قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p231/r5.claim: Abu Qatada reports the Prophet’s words at the night of the valley: God seized their souls when He willed and returned them when He willed.
DURR-FULL:v7p231/r5.anchor: عن أبي قتادة رضي الله عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لهم ليلة الوادي

DURR-FULL:v7p232/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p232/r1.speaker: أنس بن مالك
DURR-FULL:v7p232/r1.claim: Anas reports that when the travelers slept until sunrise, the Prophet described souls as entrusted in servants’ bodies, taken and sent back whenever God wills.
DURR-FULL:v7p232/r1.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك رضي الله عنه قال: كنت مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في سفر فقال

DURR-FULL:v7p232/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p232/r2.speaker: أبو أمامة
DURR-FULL:v7p232/r2.claim: Abu Umama reports that during a journey, after the Prophet and companions slept past sunrise and prayed, he invoked this verse about God taking souls in sleep and death.
DURR-FULL:v7p232/r2.anchor: عن أبي أمامة رضي الله عنه قال: كنا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في سفر فلم يستيقظ

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3252#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3252#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3252#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas distinguishes soul and spirit, likened to sunlight: in sleep God takes the soul while the spirit remains in the living body; at death He takes the spirit, or returns the soul if the person’s term is postponed.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3252#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : الله يتوفى الانفس الاية قال : نفس وروح بينهما شعاع الشمس ، فيتوفى الله النفس في منامه

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3252#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3252#2/r2.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3252#2/r2.claim: Sulaim ibn Amir reports Umar's question about why some dreams prove true and others do not; Ali explains that visions of souls held with God in heaven are true, while devils meet souls returned to bodies and tell them falsehoods. Umar marveled at the explanation.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3252#2/r2.anchor: عن سليم بن عامر ان عمر بن الخطاب قال : العجب من رؤيا الرجل انه يبيت فيرى الشيء لم يخطر له علي باله

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3252#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3252#2/r3.speaker: أبو أيوب
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3252#2/r3.claim: Abu Ayyub heard the Prophet pray before sleep, asking God to forgive him if He takes his soul and protect him if He postpones its taking.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3252#2/r3.anchor: عن أبي ايوب . انه سمع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حين كان نازلا عليه في بيته حين اراد ان يرقد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p24#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p24#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p24#2/r1.claim: ‘Those that did not die’ coordinates with ‘souls’ under the qualifying sense of ‘at their death’; ‘in their sleep’ attaches to ‘takes,’ describing souls taken nightly and then awakened.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p24#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p24#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p24#2/r2.claim: Calling sleep a taking/death is a linguistic comparison, since ordinary usage does not call a sleeper dead; sleep suspends perception while the main organs remain able to resume their functions on waking.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p24#2/r2.anchor: وهذا جار على وجه التشبيه بحسب عرف اللغة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p24#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p24#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p24#2/r3.claim: The fāʾ in ‘so He retains’ is explicative, bringing out an unstated inference required to explain the taking of souls here.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p24#2/r3.anchor: لأن ما تقدم يقتضي مقدرا يفصح عنه الفاء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p24#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p24#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p24#2/r4.claim: Imsāk is holding fast and not releasing; God keeps the soul whose death He decreed and prevents its return, figuratively sustaining the state of death, though the family may wish for revival.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p24#2/r4.anchor: والإمساك : الشد باليد وعدم تسليم المشدود

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p24#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p24#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p24#2/r5.claim: Irsāl means release and permission to return; ‘the other’ is the soul that did not die, treated as dead in sleep, and God restores its full life, highlighting the difference between the two kinds of taking.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p24#2/r5.anchor: والإرسال : الإطلاق والتمكين من مبارحة المكان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p24#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p24#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p24#2/r6.claim: ‘To an appointed term’ modifies ‘sends’; because sending means restoring life, God does not remove that life completely before its divinely assigned term. Tasmiyah means designation, as in 2:282.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p24#2/r6.anchor: لما فيه من معنى يرد الحياة إليها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p25/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p25/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p25/r1.claim: The author prefers this reading of the verse as free of strained reinterpretation, ellipsis, or شبه الاستخدام in the phrase about the soul on which death is decreed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p25/r1.anchor: هذا هو الوجه في تفسير الآية الخلي عن التكلفات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p25/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p25/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p25/r2.claim: The concluding sentence gives the result of the evidence: death and sleep reveal God’s exclusive control and right to worship; the point is reflection on divine craftsmanship and wisdom encountered daily, not merely distinguishing sleep from death.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p25/r2.anchor: أي أن في حالة الإماتة والإنامة دلائل على انفراد الله تعالى بالتصرف وأنه المستحق للعبادة دون غيره وأن ليس المقصود من هذا الخبر الإخبار باختلاف حالتي الموت والنوم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p25/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p25/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p25/r3.claim: ‘Signs’ is plural because death and sleep are two astonishing states, each involving a different divine act: death removes life and prevents its return; sleep partially withdraws life and repeatedly restores it until permanent removal.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p25/r3.anchor: لأنهما حالتان عجيبتان ثم في كل حالة تصرف يغاير التصرف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p25/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p25/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p25/r4.claim: The signs support both figurative illustration and inference to God’s exclusive control; ‘indeed’ is emphatic because most people act as though they deny the signs by ignoring their implications.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p25/r4.anchor: حاصلة على كل من إرادة التمثيل وإرادة استدلال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p25/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p25/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p25/r5.claim: Tafakkur is effortful thought: sustained mental work and repeated contemplation of how evidence points to truths.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p25/r5.anchor: معالجة الفكر ومعاودة التدبر في دلالة الأدلة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p25/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p25/r6.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p25/r6.claim: The majority read qaḍā ʿalayhā al-mawt actively, with ‘death’ as its direct object.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p25/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p25/r7.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وخلف
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p25/r7.claim: Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Khalaf read the verb passively with ‘death’ nominative, either by deleting the preposition bi- or by construing qaḍā as ‘ordained.’

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p533/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p533/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p533/r7.claim: Taking souls in sleep and death is a major sign of God's oneness and that no idol shares His power.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p533/r7.anchor: ثم نبه تعالى على آية من آياته الكبر تدل الناظر على الوحدانية وأن ذلك لا شرك فيه لصنم وهي حالة التوفي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p533/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p533/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p533/r8.claim: Complete taking of a soul is death; incomplete taking is sleep.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p533/r8.anchor: وذلك أن الله تعالى ما توفاه على الكمال فهو الذي يموت، وما توفاه متوفيا غير مكمل فهو الذي يكون في النوم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p533/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p533/r9.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p533/r9.claim: Ibn Zayd states that sleep is a death and death is a death.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p533/r9.anchor: قال ابن زيد: النوم وفاة، والموت وفاة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p533/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p533/r10.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p533/r10.claim: Some interpreters distinguish the soul from the spirit, and others distinguish a discriminating soul from an imaginative one; Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls such explanations conjectural.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p533/r10.anchor: وفرق قوم أيضا بين نفس التمييز ونفس التخيل، إلى غير ذلك من الأقوال التي هي غلبة ظن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p533/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p533/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p533/r11.claim: The exact reality of soul and spirit is among what God has kept hidden, as stated in 17:85.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p533/r11.anchor: وحقيقة الأمر في هذا هي مما استأثر الله به وغيبه عن عباده في قوله: قل الروح من أمر ربي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p533/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p533/r12.speaker: حديث بلال
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p533/r12.claim: In the authentic report of Bilāl at the valley, God took their souls when He willed and returned them when He willed.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p533/r12.anchor: في الحديث الصحيح: «إن الله قبض أرواحنا حين شاء وردها علينا حين شاء» في حديث بلال

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p534/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p534/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p534/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says detailed speculation about the soul and spirit is burdensome even though scholars have discussed it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p534/r1.anchor: فظاهر أن التفصيل والخوض في هذا كله عناء وإن كان قد تعرض القول في هذا ونحوه أئمة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p534/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p534/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p534/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is quoted as saying that a human has a soul for reason and discernment and a spirit for life and movement; in sleep God takes the soul but not the spirit.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p534/r2.anchor: ذكره الثعلبي وغيره عن ابن عباس أنه قال: في ابن آدم نفس بها العقل والتمييز، وفيه روح به النفس والتحرك، فإذا نام العبد قبض الله نفسه ولم يقبض روحه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p534/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p534/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p534/r3.claim: The appointed term is each person's lifespan.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p534/r3.anchor: والأجل المسمى في هذه الآية: هو عمر كل إنسان

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p534/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p534/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p534/r4.claim: Most readers have qaḍā ʿalayhā in the active voice with fatḥa on qāf; Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, Ibn Waththāb, Ṭalḥa, al-Aʿmash, and ʿĪsā read the passive quḍiya with ḍamma.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p534/r4.anchor: وقرأ جمهور القراء: «قضى عليها» بفتح القاف على بناء الفعل للفاعل. وقرأ حمزة والكسائي «قضي» بضم القاف على بنائه للمفعول

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p534/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p534/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p534/r5.claim: Reflecting on this power shows that only the One, the Self-Sufficient can control it; there is no other lord.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p534/r5.anchor: ثم أحال أهل الفكرة على النظر في هذا ونحوه فإنه من البين أن هذه القدرة لا يملكها ويصرفها إلا الواحد الصمد، لا رب غيره

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p185#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p185#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p185#3/r1.claim: At bodily death, God takes the spirits when their bodies die.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p185#3/r1.anchor: أي يقبض الأرواح حين موت أجسادها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p185#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p185#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p185#3/r2.claim: God also takes the souls of those who have not died, during their sleep.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p185#3/r2.anchor: ﴿ والتي لم تمت ﴾ أي ويتوفى التي لم تمت ﴿ في منامها ﴾

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p185#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p185#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p185#3/r3.claim: He withholds from the body and soul the one on whom death has been decreed.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p185#3/r3.anchor: ﴿ فيمسك ﴾ أي عن الجسد والنفس ﴿ التي قضى عليها الموت ﴾

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p185#3/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p185#3/r4.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p185#3/r4.claim: Hamza and al-Kisa'i read the verb passively and put al-mawt in the nominative.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p185#3/r4.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي قضي بضم القاف وفتح الياء الموت بالرفع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p185#3/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p185#3/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p185#3/r5.claim: God sends the other soul back to the body until the end of its lifespan.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p185#3/r5.anchor: ﴿ ويرسل الأخرى ﴾ إلى الجسد ﴿ إلى أجل مسمى ﴾

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p185#3/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p185#3/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p185#3/r6.claim: These signs prompt reflection on resurrection.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p185#3/r6.anchor: ﴿ إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يتفكرون ﴾ في أمر البعث

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p185#3/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p185#3/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p185#3/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says living and dead souls meet in sleep, recognize and question one another, then the living souls return to their bodies.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p185#3/r7.anchor: وروى سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس قال تلتقي أرواح الأحياء وأرواح الأموات في المنام

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p185#3/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p185#3/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p185#3/r8.claim: In another report, a person has a nafs for intellect and discernment and a ruh for life and movement; sleep takes the nafs but not the ruh.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p185#3/r8.anchor: وقال ابن عباس في رواية أخرى في ابن آدم نفس وروح فبالنفس العقل والتمييز

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p185#3/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p185#3/r9.speaker: ابن جريج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p185#3/r9.claim: Ibn Jurayj distinguishes a nafs from a ruh: God takes the nafs in sleep and returns it on waking; when death is intended, it is not returned and the ruh is taken.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p185#3/r9.anchor: وقال ابن جريج في الغنسان روح ونفس بينهما حاجز فهو تعالى يقبض النفس عند النوم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p185#3/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p185#3/r10.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p185#3/r10.claim: Scholars differ in two views over whether nafs and ruh are distinct; Ibn al-Jawzi refers elsewhere for their details.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p185#3/r10.anchor: وقد اختلف العلماء هل بين النفس والروح فرق على قولين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p185#3/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p185#3/r11.speaker: الفراء وابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p185#3/r11.claim: They take the sleeper's tawaffi as sleep itself: the nafs is restrained from acting and released to act upon waking.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p185#3/r11.anchor: وهذا اختيار الفراء وابن الأنباري فعلى هذا يكون معنى توفي النائم قبض نفسه عن التصرف

BURSEVI:v8p85/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p85/r1.speaker: القاموس
BURSEVI:v8p85/r1.claim: Al-Qamus glosses توفاه الله as God taking or receiving the person's spirit.

BURSEVI:v8p85/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p85/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p85/r2.claim: Al-anfus is the plural of nafs and here denotes the speaking human soul, called by religious scholars the additional human sovereign spirit.
BURSEVI:v8p85/r2.anchor: جمع نفس بسكون الفاء ، وهي النفس الناطقة المسماة عند أهل الشرع

BURSEVI:v8p85/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p85/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p85/r3.claim: It is called nafs because it is attached to the body and subject to bodily governance, and rūḥ because it is immaterial in itself and returns to God.
BURSEVI:v8p85/r3.anchor: فسميت نفسا باعتبار تعلقها بالبدن وانصياعها بأحكامه

BURSEVI:v8p85/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p85/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p85/r4.claim: Bursevi characterizes the soul as lower and human, and the spirit as higher and divine.
BURSEVI:v8p85/r4.anchor: فالنفس ناسوتية سفلية والروح لاهوتية علوية

BURSEVI:v8p85/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p85/r5.speaker: قالوا
BURSEVI:v8p85/r5.claim: The human spirit is a simple substance that moves the body through governance and control, rather than inhering in it by either kind of indwelling.
BURSEVI:v8p85/r5.anchor: قالوا : الروح الإنساني جوهر بسيط محرك للجسم

BURSEVI:v8p85/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p85/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p85/r6.claim: The animal spirit is an effect of the human spirit, like the moon receiving light from the sun; animals share it, and medicine works to regulate and strengthen it.
BURSEVI:v8p85/r6.anchor: والروح الحيواني أثر من آثار هذا الروح على ما سبق

BURSEVI:v8p85/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p85/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p85/r7.claim: The animal spirit does not bear the trust, knowledge, or faith; its ordinary bodily locus is eaten by earth, unlike the bodies of prophets, the truthful, and martyrs.
BURSEVI:v8p85/r7.anchor: ولا يحمل الأمانة والمعرفة والتراب يأكل محله

BURSEVI:v8p85/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p85/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p85/r8.claim: The human spirit bears the trust, knowledge, and faith, is cultivated by the sciences of religious and spiritual truth through divine sages, and is not eaten by earth.
BURSEVI:v8p85/r8.anchor: فإنه حامل الأمانة والمعرفة والإيمان ويتصرف فيه علم الشريعة

BURSEVI:v8p85/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p85/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p85/r9.claim: As nafs, the human spirit is the prophet or saint, the self meant by I, and the one placed in the grave, questioned, rewarded, or punished after separating from the body.
BURSEVI:v8p85/r9.anchor: وهو باعتبار كونه نفسا هو النبي والولي والمشار إليه بأنا

BURSEVI:v8p85/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p85/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p85/r10.claim: The body's sole relation to the human spirit is as an instrument for gaining knowledge through the senses; like a hunter's net, its loss after the catch is a relief from weight.
BURSEVI:v8p85/r10.anchor: وليس له علاقة مع البدن سوى أن يستعمله في كسب المعارف

BURSEVI:v8p85/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p85/r11.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v8p85/r11.claim: The Prophet calls death a believer's gift; Bursevi explains that the body's instrument is a gain to lose once spiritual harvest is complete.
BURSEVI:v8p85/r11.anchor: نعم بطلت الشبكة بعد الفراغ من الصيد ، فبطلانها غنيمة

BURSEVI:v8p85/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p85/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p85/r12.claim: If the bodily instrument fails before spiritual harvest, the result is regret, as in the doomed person's plea to return and do good.
BURSEVI:v8p85/r12.anchor: أما لو بطلت الشبكة قبل الصيد ، فقد عظمت فيه الحسرة والندامة

BURSEVI:v8p85#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p85#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p85#2/r1.claim: Death is the disappearance of sensory power, while life is its presence; animal life begins with the animal spirit.
BURSEVI:v8p85#2/r1.anchor: والموت : زوال القوة الحساسة كما أن الحياة وجود هذه القوة

BURSEVI:v8p85#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p85#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p85#2/r2.claim: The animal spirit is located in the brain and the human spirit in the pineal heart, though this does not entail containment there; Sunnis hold human spirits spatially located.
BURSEVI:v8p85#2/r2.anchor: ومبدأ هذه القوة هو الروح الحيواني الذي محله الدماغ

BURSEVI:v8p85#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p85#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p85#2/r3.claim: A living person is human in the literal sense; after death, only metaphorically so, because humanity in truth depended on the now-separated human spirit.
BURSEVI:v8p85#2/r3.anchor: ثم إن الإنسان ما دام حيا ، فهو إنسان بالحقيقة

BURSEVI:v8p85#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p85#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p85#2/r4.claim: A Mathnawi couplet illustrates that the soul is independent of bodily features and that a body without soul is a corpse.
BURSEVI:v8p85#2/r4.anchor: وفي المثنوي : جان زريش وسبلت تن فارغست

BURSEVI:v8p85#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p85#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p85#2/r5.claim: At death God ends the human spirit's outward and inward relation to its body; sensation and movement cease, the body becomes like dry wood, and reason, faith, and knowledge depart with the spirit.
BURSEVI:v8p85#2/r5.anchor: ومعنى الآية : يقبض الله الأرواح الإنسانية عن الأبدان

BURSEVI:v8p85#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p85#2/r6.speaker: الوسيط
BURSEVI:v8p85#2/r6.claim: Al-Wasit reads حين موتها as حين موت أبدانها, with the genitive complement omitted.
BURSEVI:v8p85#2/r6.anchor: وفي "الوسيط" : {حين موتها} ؛ أي : حين موت أبدانها

BURSEVI:v8p85#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p85#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p85#2/r7.claim: Bursevi says this apparent wording conflicts with 3:185, which says every soul tastes death; he resolves it as God taking spirits when bodies die by separation.
BURSEVI:v8p85#2/r7.anchor: يقول الفقير : ظاهره يخالف قوله تعالى : {كل نفس ذآااقة الموت}

BURSEVI:v8p85#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p85#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p85#2/r8.claim: God is credited with taking souls because he commands the angels who carry out the seizure.
BURSEVI:v8p85#2/r8.anchor: اللهم إلا أن يقال : المراد أن الله يتوفى الأرواح حين موت أبدانها

BURSEVI:v8p85#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p85#2/r9.speaker: زهرة الرياض
BURSEVI:v8p85#2/r9.claim: Zahrat al-Riyad says God orders the spirit to leave, which even gathered angels could not extract on their own; an assisting angel handles it, and the Angel of Death receives it at the throat in faith or unbelief.
BURSEVI:v8p85#2/r9.anchor: وفي "زهرة الرياض" : التوفي من الله الأمر بخروج الروح من البدن

BURSEVI:v8p85#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p85#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p85#2/r10.claim: Bursevi reports that God directly took Fatima's soul when she would not accept the Angel of Death, whereas the Angel of Death took the Prophet's soul because he was the community's leader.
BURSEVI:v8p85#2/r10.anchor: على أن من خواص العباد من يتولى الله قبض روحه

BURSEVI:v8p85#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p85#2/r11.speaker: ذو النون المصري
BURSEVI:v8p85#2/r11.claim: Dhu al-Nun prays that God personally take his soul, honor him, and punish him rather than entrusting those acts to the angels of death, Paradise, or Hell.
BURSEVI:v8p85#2/r11.anchor: وكما قال ذو النون المصري قدس سره : إلهي لا تكلني إلى ملك الموت

BURSEVI:v8p86/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p86/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p86/r1.claim: The phrase in its sleep is syntactically attached to an understood occurrence of يتوفى.

BURSEVI:v8p86/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p86/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p86/r2.claim: Sleep is the relaxation of the brain's nerves by moist vapors rising to it.
BURSEVI:v8p86/r2.anchor: المنام والنوم واحد ، وهو استرخاء أعصاب الدماغ

BURSEVI:v8p86/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p86/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p86/r3.claim: The reported definitions that God takes the soul without death, that sleep is a light death, and that death is deep sleep are all valid from different perspectives.
BURSEVI:v8p86/r3.anchor: وقيل : هو أن يتوفى الله النفس من غير موت كما في الآية

BURSEVI:v8p86/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p86/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p86/r4.claim: In sleep God severs the soul's outward bodily control but not its inward relation; breath and movement continue through the animal spirit while reason and discrimination disappear with the human spirit.
BURSEVI:v8p86/r4.anchor: ويتوفى الأنفس التي لم تمت في منامها ؛ أي : يتوفاها

BURSEVI:v8p86/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p86/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p86/r5.claim: Sufis compare sleep to spiritual shedding or departure; the corresponding state while awake is stronger in spiritual state and witnessing than the sleeper's.
BURSEVI:v8p86/r5.anchor: ومثل النوم حال الانسلاخ عند الصوفية إلا أن المنسلخ حال اليقظة أقوى حالا وشهودا من المنسلخ حال النوم

BURSEVI:v8p86/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p86/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p86/r6.claim: Death and sleep are both called taking because sleepers resemble the dead in lacking discernment; a transmitted saying calls sleep the brother of death.
BURSEVI:v8p86/r6.anchor: وعبر عن الموت ، والنوم بالتوفي تشبيها للنائمين بالموتى

BURSEVI:v8p86/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p86/r7.speaker: علي رضي الله عنه
BURSEVI:v8p86/r7.claim: Ali reports that the soul leaves during sleep while a ray remains in the body to make dreams possible, and returns faster than a moment upon waking.
BURSEVI:v8p86/r7.anchor: وعن علي رضي الله عنه أن الروح يخرج عند النوم ويبقى شعاعه في الجسد

BURSEVI:v8p86/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p86/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p86/r8.claim: A report says believers' spirits ascend in sleep; those ritually pure may prostrate beneath the Throne, so sleeping in ablution is recommended for true dreams and divine converse.
BURSEVI:v8p86/r8.anchor: ويروى : أن أرواح المؤمنين تعرج عند النوم إلى السماء

BURSEVI:v8p86/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p86/r9.speaker: قال بعضهم
BURSEVI:v8p86/r9.claim: Some say spirits are subtle and bodies dense; sleep and spiritual shedding let spirits travel the unseen realm, renew their witnessing, and increase longing for nearness to God.
BURSEVI:v8p86/r9.anchor: قال بعضهم : خلق الله الأرواح على اللطافة والأجساد على الكثافة

BURSEVI:v8p86/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p86/r10.speaker: قال بعضهم
BURSEVI:v8p86/r10.claim: The same speaker says sleep is pleasurable because the servant is in God's merciful care, whereas death is painful because the servant is in the Angel of Death's hand.
BURSEVI:v8p86/r10.anchor: وإنما يستريح العبد ويجد اللذة في النوم ؛ لأنه في يد الله

BURSEVI:v8p86#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p86#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p86#2/r1.claim: Imsak means to hold and preserve, and qada means to decree; God keeps the souls of the dead and does not return them to their bodies.
BURSEVI:v8p86#2/r1.anchor: إمساك شيء تعلق به وحفظه ، والقضاء الحكم

BURSEVI:v8p86#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p86#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p86#2/r2.claim: The dead remain in the later barzakh, the realm after separation from worldly life, distinct from the imaginal barzakh between immaterial spirits and bodies entered through sleep or spiritual shedding.
BURSEVI:v8p86#2/r2.anchor: وذلك الإمساك إنما هو عالم البرزخ الذي تكون الأرواح فيه بعد المفارقة

BURSEVI:v8p86#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p86#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p86#2/r3.claim: The stages before worldly life belong to the descending arc and have priority, while those after it belong to the ascending arc and have finality.
BURSEVI:v8p86#2/r3.anchor: لأن مراتب تنزلات الوجود ومعارجه دورية والمرتبة التي قبل النشأة الدنيوية هي من مراتب التنزلات ولها الأولية والتي بعدها هي من مراتب المعارج

BURSEVI:v8p86#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p86#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p86#2/r4.claim: Forms in the later barzakh reflect deeds and their results from earthly life; the earlier barzakh's forms do not, and neither realm is identical with the afterlife, though both are luminous, immaterial spiritual worlds of images.
BURSEVI:v8p86#2/r4.anchor: الصور التي تلحق الأرواح في البرزخ الأخير ؛ إنما هي صور الأعمال ونتائج الأفعال

BURSEVI:v8p86#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p86#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p86#3/r1.claim: God sends the souls of the living, sleeping people, back to their bodies when they wake and descend from the bounded imaginal realm.
BURSEVI:v8p86#3/r1.anchor: ويرسل أنفس الأحياء ، وهي النائمة إلى أبدانها عند اليقظة

BURSEVI:v8p86#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p86#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p86#3/r2.claim: The imaginal realm is like bodily substance in being perceptible and measurable, and like intellectual substance in luminosity; it mediates between them so forms first become embodied and then dense.
BURSEVI:v8p86#3/r2.anchor: والعالم المثال شبه بالجوهر الجسماني في كونه محسوسا مقداريا

BURSEVI:v8p86#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p86#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p86#3/r3.claim: An abstract thing such as knowledge takes on an imaginal form.
BURSEVI:v8p86#3/r3.anchor: ألا ترى أن حقيقة العلم الذي هو مجرد يتجسد بالصورة التي في عالم المثال

BURSEVI:v8p86#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p86#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p86#3/r4.claim: The appointed term is the set time of death and describes the general span of sending souls, not each instance, which would wrongly imply no sending after the first waking.
BURSEVI:v8p86#3/r4.anchor: هو الوقت المضروب لموتها ، وهو غاية لجنس الإرسال

BURSEVI:v8p86#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p86#3/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
BURSEVI:v8p86#3/r5.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says the spirits of living and dead people meet in dreams and recognize one another as God wills; the dead are held, while the living return to their bodies until life's end.
BURSEVI:v8p86#3/r5.anchor: وعن سعيد بن جبير أن أرواح الأحياء وأرواح الأموات تلتقي في المنام

BURSEVI:v8p86#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p86#3/r6.speaker: الأسئلة المقحمة
BURSEVI:v8p86#3/r6.claim: Al-Asʾila al-Muqḥima explains that the spirit is taken during sleep and kept if its owner's appointed death coincides with that sleep.
BURSEVI:v8p86#3/r6.anchor: وفي "الأسئلة المقحمة" : يقبض الروح حال النوم ، ثم يمسك الروح

BURSEVI:v8p86#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p86#3/r7.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v8p86#3/r7.claim: A Prophetic bedtime prayer asks God to have mercy if he keeps the sleeper's soul and to protect it if he sends it back; Bursevi says this supports reading the holding clause as following the sleep clause.
BURSEVI:v8p86#3/r7.anchor: ويؤيده قوله عليه السلام : "إذا أوى أحدكم إلى فراشه فلينفض فراشه بداخلة إزاره

BURSEVI:v8p86#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p86#3/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p86#3/r8.claim: The prayer signals that the purpose of life is righteousness and all else should serve as a means to it.
BURSEVI:v8p86#3/r8.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى أن المقصود من الحياة هو : الصلاح

BURSEVI:v8p87/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p87/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p87/r1.claim: The signs concern God's two ways of taking souls, holding them in death and sending them back in sleep, and show the perfection of his power, wisdom, and encompassing mercy.
BURSEVI:v8p87/r1.anchor: فيما ذكر من التوفي على الوجهين والإمساك في أحدهما

BURSEVI:v8p87/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p87/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p87/r2.claim: Reflection on souls' complete departure at death, their survival after bodily decay, and their partial departure in sleep reveals what leads to happiness or misery and how souls return until their terms end.
BURSEVI:v8p87/r2.anchor: في كيفية تعلق الأرواح بالأبدان وتوفيها عنها تارة بالكلية كما عند الموت

BURSEVI:v8p87/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p87/r3.speaker: الكواشي والكاشفي
BURSEVI:v8p87/r3.claim: Al-Kawashi and al-Kashifi say reflection on death as sleep and resurrection as waking proves that the one able to take and restore souls can resurrect; the Torah similarly addresses humanity as children of Adam.
BURSEVI:v8p87/r3.anchor: {لقوم يتفكرون} ، فيستدلون على أن القادر على ذلك قادر على البعث

BURSEVI:v8p87/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p87/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p87/r4.claim: A Persian poetic line calls death a door through which everyone must pass.

BURSEVI:v8p87/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p87/r5.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v8p87/r5.claim: A sacred report says God has no hesitation in an act he will do like his hesitation in taking the soul of a believing servant.
BURSEVI:v8p87/r5.anchor: ما ترددت في شيء أنا فاعله كترددي في قبض نفس عبدي المؤمن

BURSEVI:v8p87/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p87/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p87/r6.claim: Because divine hesitation cannot mean perplexity or ignorance about what is best, it signifies a pause: God shows the believer the blessings prepared for him until he longs for death and meeting God.
BURSEVI:v8p87/r6.anchor: لما كان التردد ، وهو التحير بين الشيئين لعدم العلم

BURSEVI:v8p87/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p87/r7.speaker: شرح السنة
BURSEVI:v8p87/r7.claim: Another explanation is that God repeatedly sends causes of harm such as hunger and illness, withholds their fatal effect, and repeats them until the believer welcomes death; the phrase about hating death answers an objection by referring to death's severity, not aversion to meeting God.
BURSEVI:v8p87/r7.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد من تردده تعالى إرسال أسباب الهلاك إلى المؤمن

BURSEVI:v8p87/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p87/r8.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v8p87/r8.claim: A Prophetic report says that no one will see his Lord before he dies.
BURSEVI:v8p87/r8.anchor: إن أحدكم لن يرى ربه حتى يموت

BURSEVI:v8p87/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p87/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p87/r9.claim: Persian couplets say one who has not fully died from existence cannot behold God, and that dying before death brings security.
BURSEVI:v8p87/r9.anchor: تانميرد بنده ازهستى تمام أو نبيند حق تعالى والسلام مرك بيش از مرك امنست اى فتى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p101#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p101#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p101#2/r4.claim: God governs existence as He wills and takes souls at major death through the angels who extract them from bodies, and at minor death during sleep.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p101#2/r4.anchor: يتوفى الأنفس الوفاة الكبرى، بما يرسل من الحفظة الذين يقبضونها من الأبدان، والوفاة الصغرى عند المنام

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p101#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p101#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p101#2/r5.claim: An'am 60–61 presents minor sleep-death before major death, whereas this verse mentions major death first and then sleep.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p101#2/r5.anchor: فذكر الوفاتين: الصغرى ثم الكبرى. وفي هذه الآية ذكر الكبرى ثم الصغرى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p101#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p101#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p101#2/r6.claim: The verse indicates that souls meet in the highest assembly, as related in a prophetic report cited by Ibn Mandah and others.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p101#2/r6.anchor: فيه دلالة على أنها تجتمع في الملأ الأعلى، كما ورد بذلك الحديث المرفوع الذي رواه ابن منده وغيره

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p101#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p101#2/r7.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p101#2/r7.claim: The Prophet taught a bedtime prayer asking God for mercy if He holds one's soul and protection if He sends it back, after advising one to dust the bed with an inner garment.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p101#2/r7.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "إذا أوى أحدكم إلى فراشه فلينفضه بداخلة إزاره،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p101#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p101#2/r8.speaker: بعض السلف
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p101#2/r8.claim: Some early authorities say God takes the dead person's spirit at death and the living person's spirit during sleep; the souls recognize one another as God wills.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p101#2/r8.anchor: وقال بعض السلف [رحمهم الله] (2) يقبض أرواح الأموات إذا ماتوا، وأرواح الأحياء إذا ناموا، فتتعارف

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p102/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p102/r1.speaker: السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p102/r1.claim: Al-Suddi says the surviving soul is sent back until the remainder of its appointed term.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p102/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p102/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p102/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas explains that God retains the souls of the dead and sends back those of the living without error.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p102/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: يمسك أنفس الأموات، ويرسل أنفس الأحياء، ولا يغلط

JISHUMI:v8p6072/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6072/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6072/r7.claim: Worship is due to the Creator of blessings, not to one who can neither benefit nor harm.
JISHUMI:v8p6072/r7.anchor: تدل الآيات أن العبادة تستحق لخالق النعم دون من لا ينفع، ولا يضر.

JISHUMI:v8p6072/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6072/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6072/r8.claim: The verses establish that argumentation in religion is valid.
JISHUMI:v8p6072/r8.anchor: وتدل على صحة الحجاج في الدين.

JISHUMI:v8p6072/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6072/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6072/r9.claim: The book was sent down to be conveyed and to command action; God intended guidance by it rather than misguidance.
JISHUMI:v8p6072/r9.anchor: وتدل أنه أنزل الكتاب ليبلغه ويأمر بالعمل به، وأنه أراد الاهتداء به دون الإضلال.

JISHUMI:v8p6072/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6072/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6072/r10.claim: The author says guidance and misguidance are human acts, in keeping with his theological position.
JISHUMI:v8p6072/r10.anchor: وتدل أن الهداية والضلال فعلهم على ما نقوله

JISHUMI:v8p6072/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6072/r11.speaker: حمزة والكسائي والأعمش
JISHUMI:v8p6072/r11.claim: Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and al-Aʿmash read the passive form and put “death” in the nominative.
JISHUMI:v8p6072/r11.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي والأعمش: قضي بضم القاف وكسر الضاد وفتح الياء على ما لم يسم فاعله، الموت رفع.

JISHUMI:v8p6072/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6072/r12.speaker: الباقون
JISHUMI:v8p6072/r12.claim: The other readers use the active form and put “death” in the accusative.
JISHUMI:v8p6072/r12.anchor: الباقون بفتح القاف والضاد وسكون الياء، الموت بالنصب

JISHUMI:v8p6072/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6072/r13.speaker: أبو عبيد وأبو حاتم
JISHUMI:v8p6072/r13.claim: Abū ʿUbayd and Abū Ḥātim prefer the active reading because God is explicitly the one who takes the souls.
JISHUMI:v8p6072/r13.anchor: واختاره أبو عبيد وأبو حاتم لقوله: (الله يتوفى الأنفس) فهو يقضى عليها

JISHUMI:v8p6072/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6072/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6072/r14.claim: Tawaffī is taking something completely; the verb can also mean fully receiving something from someone.
JISHUMI:v8p6072/r14.anchor: التوفي: قبض الشيء على التمام، يقال: توفيت من فلان، واستوفيت بمعنى

JISHUMI:v8p6072/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6072/r15.speaker: الفراء
JISHUMI:v8p6072/r15.claim: Al-Farrāʾ explains “I am taking you” in 3:55 as taking Jesus from earth without death.
JISHUMI:v8p6072/r15.anchor: قال الفراء: إني قابضك من الأرض بغير موت

JISHUMI:v8p6072/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6072/r16.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p6072/r16.claim: One view says life and death are two alternating accidents, which only God can bring about.
JISHUMI:v8p6072/r16.anchor: وقيل: هما عرضان يتعاقبان، لا يقدر عليها غير الله

JISHUMI:v8p6072/r17.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6072/r17.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p6072/r17.claim: Another account describes life as an accident while necessary knowledge departs but life and spirit remain; death's seizure is incompatible with life.
JISHUMI:v8p6072/r17.anchor: وقيل: الحياة عرض، وذهاب العلوم الضرورية، وتبقى معه الحياة والروح، وقبض الموت ينافي الحياة.

JISHUMI:v8p6073/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6073/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6073/r1.claim: The verse connects to “you are not their guardian”: God guards them, takes them in sleep, restores them on waking, and gives life and death.
JISHUMI:v8p6073/r1.anchor: أن الحفيظ عليهم من يتوفاهم ويصرفهم كيف يشاء، ويقبضهم في النوم، ويبعثهم في اليقظة

JISHUMI:v8p6073/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6073/r2.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v8p6073/r2.claim: Abū Muslim connects the verse to 39:36: God suffices Muḥammad, while idols cannot manage anything for their worshippers.
JISHUMI:v8p6073/r2.anchor: وقيل: يتصل بقوله: (أليس الله بكاف عبده) تقديره: هو أقدر أم ما أعدوه، فهو يكفيك أمرهم، وهي لا تكفي لهم أمرا، عن أبي مسلم

JISHUMI:v8p6073/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6073/r3.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p6073/r3.claim: Another connection is to 39:38: the Creator and owner of life and death alone deserves worship.
JISHUMI:v8p6073/r3.anchor: وقيل: يتصل بقوله: (ولئن سألتهم) بين أن المستحق للعبادة خالق السماوات والأرض، ومالك النفع والضر والموت والحياة

JISHUMI:v8p6073/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6073/r7.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p6073/r7.claim: The wording may urge reflection so people recognize their practice is worthless and God alone is eternal.
JISHUMI:v8p6073/r7.anchor: وقيل: بقوله: (يتفكرون) أي: هلا تفكروا فعلموا أن ما هم عليه ليس بشيء، وأن القديم هو الله الواحد

JISHUMI:v8p6073/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6073/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6073/r8.claim: God takes souls from their capacity to act and retains them; sending a soul back is the opposite of taking it.
JISHUMI:v8p6073/r8.anchor: الله يتوفى الأنفس يعني: يقبضها عن التصرف ويمسكها ويحبسها، ويدل عليه أنه جعل الإرسال ضد التوفي

JISHUMI:v8p6073/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6073/r9.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p6073/r9.claim: At death, God retains the soul when its appointed term ends by removing life and spirit.
JISHUMI:v8p6073/r9.anchor: قيل: إن المراد بالتوفي الإمساك والحبس حين موتها يعني: وقت موتها وانقضاء أجلها بإخراج الحياة والروح

JISHUMI:v8p6073/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6073/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6073/r10.claim: God also seizes the soul of one who has not died during sleep, keeping it from acting.
JISHUMI:v8p6073/r10.anchor: والتي لم تمت في منامها يعني ويقبض التي لم تمت في منامها، فيحبسها عن التصرف

JISHUMI:v8p6073/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6073/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6073/r11.claim: God retains the soul whose death He decreed until Resurrection; it does not return to worldly life.
JISHUMI:v8p6073/r11.anchor: فيمسك التي قضى عليها الموت إلى يوم القيامة لا تعود إلى الدنيا

JISHUMI:v8p6073/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6073/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6073/r12.claim: God sends the sleeping soul back until its appointed time of death.
JISHUMI:v8p6073/r12.anchor: ويرسل الأخرى يعني: النائم إلى أجل مسمى إلى وقت سمي لموته

JISHUMI:v8p6073/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6073/r13.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p6073/r13.claim: An alternative analysis puts the sequence out of order: God takes souls at death and retains them, while sleepers live to their term.
