JISHUMI:v8p6073/r13.anchor: وقيل: في الآية تقديم وتأخير، وتقديره: الله يتوفى الأنفس حين موتها فيمسك، والتي لم تمت في منامها تعيش إلى انتهاء أجلها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p133#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p133#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p133#2/r1.claim: Al-anfus means whole persons; taking them means causing death by removing the health and integrity that let their parts live, sense, and perceive.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p133#2/r1.anchor: وتوفيها : إماتتها ، وهو أن يسلب ما هي به حية

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p133#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p133#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p133#2/r2.claim: Death is like the removal of a person’s whole self when the health of its parts is taken away.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p133#2/r2.anchor: هو أن يسلب ما هي به حية حساسة دراكة : من صحة أجزائها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p133#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p133#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p133#2/r3.claim: God takes the souls of sleepers as they sleep, likening them to the dead because they cannot distinguish or act; compare 6:60.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p133#2/r3.anchor: يريد ويتوفى الأنفس التي لم تمت في منامها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p133#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p133#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p133#2/r4.claim: Sleepers cannot distinguish or act, just as the dead cannot.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p133#2/r4.anchor: حيث لا يميزون ولا يتصرفون ، كما أن الموتى كذلك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p133#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p133#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p133#2/r5.claim: God retains the souls whose true death He has decreed and does not restore them to life at that time.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p133#2/r5.anchor: الأنفس { التي قضى عليها الموت } الحقيقي

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p133#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p133#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p133#2/r6.claim: He releases the sleeping soul until the appointed time of its death.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p133#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p133#2/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p133#2/r7.claim: An alternative distinguishes the life-and-motion spirit from the soul of intellect and discernment, saying sleep takes the latter while breathing continues through the former.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p133#2/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p133#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p133#2/r8.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās says a person has a discerning soul and a spirit for breathing and movement; God takes the soul in sleep but not the spirit.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p133#2/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في ابن آدم : نفس وروح

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p133#2/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p133#2/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p133#2/r9.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī rejects that distinction: the verse predicates death and sleep of the same whole person, while the proposed faculties are not themselves described as dying or sleeping.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p133#2/r9.anchor: والصحيح ما ذكرت أولا ، لأن الله عز وعلا علق التوفي والموت والمنام جميعا بالأنفس

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p133#2/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p133#2/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p133#2/r10.claim: The taking, retaining, and releasing of souls are signs of God’s power and knowledge for people who reflect and draw a lesson.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p133#2/r10.anchor: إن في توفي الأنفس مائتة ونائمة وإمساكها وإرسالها إلى أجل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p133#2/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p133#2/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p133#2/r11.claim: A variant reads the phrase with passive voice: death was decreed against it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p133#2/r11.anchor: قرىء : ( قضي عليها الموت ) على البناء للمفعول

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p128/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p128/r1.speaker: ابن عيسى
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p128/r1.claim: Ibn Isa says God takes souls from bodies at death; in sleep He takes ability to act while spirits remain.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p128/r1.anchor: أن الله عند توفي الأنفس يقبض أرواحها من أجسادها والتي لم تمت وهي في منامها يقبضها عن التصرف

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p128/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p128/r2.speaker: ابن عيسى
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p128/r2.claim: Ibn Isa says God holds the deceased soul from return and releases the sleeper until death.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p128/r2.anchor: إلى أجل موتها , قاله ابن عيسى

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p128/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p128/r3.speaker: ابن جريج عن ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p128/r3.claim: Ibn Jurayj transmits Ibn Abbas's view that each body has a soul and spirit; sleep takes the soul but leaves the spirit.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p128/r3.anchor: ما حكاه ابن جريج عن ابن عباس أن لكل جسد نفسا وروحا

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p128/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p128/r4.speaker: ابن جريج عن ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p128/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says God prevents the death-bound soul returning and takes its spirit; the sleeping soul returns to reunite with its spirit.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p128/r4.anchor: ما حكاه ابن جريج عن ابن عباس أن لكل جسد نفسا وروحا

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p128/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p128/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p128/r5.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says God takes dead souls at death and living souls in sleep; they meet as God wills.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p128/r5.anchor: الثالث : قاله سعيد بن جبير إن الله تعالى يقبض أرواح الموتى إذا ماتوا

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p128/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p128/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p128/r6.claim: Sa'id says God withholds the death-bound soul and returns the other to its body.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p128/r6.anchor: الثالث : قاله سعيد بن جبير إن الله تعالى يقبض أرواح الموتى

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p128/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p128/r7.speaker: علي
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p128/r7.claim: Ali says visions before a soul's return from heaven are true dreams; afterward but before it settles they are satanic falsehoods.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p128/r7.anchor: قال علي رضي الله عنه : فما رأته نفس النائم وهي في السماء قبل إرسالها إلى جسدها فهي الرؤيا الصادقة

MUQATIL:39:41-43/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:39:41-43/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:39:41-43/r4.claim: God takes each soul when its appointed term arrives, meaning the soul for which He decreed death.
MUQATIL:39:41-43/r4.anchor: يقول: عند أجلها، يعنى التى قضى الله عليها الموت

MUQATIL:39:41-43/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:39:41-43/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:39:41-43/r5.claim: The soul that has not died is the other soul, which God returns to the body.
MUQATIL:39:41-43/r5.anchor: والتي لم تمت في منامها } فتلك الأخرى التى يرسلها إلى الجسد

MUQATIL:39:41-43/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:39:41-43/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:39:41-43/r6.claim: These signs prompt reflection on resurrection.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p56#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p56#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p56#3/r1.claim: Al-anfus are the selves as they are; taking them at death means causing death by removing what makes them alive, sentient, and aware.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p56#3/r1.anchor: الأنفس الجمل كما هي وتوفيها اماتتها وهو أن يسلب ما هي به حية حساسة دراكة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p56#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p56#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p56#3/r2.claim: God takes the selves that have not died while they sleep, comparing sleepers to the dead because they neither distinguish nor act; another verse says He takes you at night.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p56#3/r2.anchor: أي يتوفاها حين تنام تشبيها للقائمين بالموتى حيث لا يميزون ولا يتصرفون كما أن الموتى كذلك

NASAFI-FULL:v4p56#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p56#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p56#3/r3.claim: God retains the selves for which He decreed real death and does not return them alive at their appointed time.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p56#3/r3.anchor: ﴿ عليها الموت ﴾ الحقيقي أى لا يردها في وقتها حية

NASAFI-FULL:v4p56#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p56#3/r4.speaker: حمزة وعلى
NASAFI-FULL:v4p56#3/r4.claim: Ḥamza and ʿAlī read qaḍā with the form shown in the commentary.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p56#3/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p56#3/r5.speaker: قيل
NASAFI-FULL:v4p56#3/r5.claim: Another account distinguishes a life-soul, which departs at death, from a discernment-soul, which departs in sleep; the sleeper continues to breathe, so sleep takes discernment rather than life.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p56#3/r5.anchor: قالوا التي تتوفى في المنام هي نفس التمييز لا نفس الحياة لأن نفس الحياة إذا زالت زال معها النفس والنائم يتنفس

NASAFI-FULL:v4p56#3/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p56#3/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
NASAFI-FULL:v4p56#3/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās compares the two selves in a human to a ray between soul and spirit: the self gives reason and discernment, while the spirit gives breath and movement; in sleep God takes the self but not the spirit.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p56#3/r6.anchor: وروى عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في ابن آدم نفس روح بينهما شعاع مثل شعاع الشمس فالنفس هي التي بها العقل والتمييز

NASAFI-FULL:v4p56#3/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p56#3/r7.speaker: علي
NASAFI-FULL:v4p56#3/r7.claim: ʿAlī says the spirit leaves during sleep, leaving its ray in the body so dreams occur, then returns faster than a moment when the sleeper wakes.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p56#3/r7.anchor: وعن علي رضي الله عنه قال تخرج الروح عند النوم ويبقى شعاعها في الجسد فبذلك يرى الرؤيا فإذا انتبه من النوم عاد الروح إلى جسده

NASAFI-FULL:v4p56#3/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p56#3/r8.speaker: علي
NASAFI-FULL:v4p56#3/r8.claim: ʿAlī says what a sleeper's self sees in heaven is a true dream, while what it sees after being sent back is a lie prompted by Satan.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p56#3/r8.anchor: وعنه ما رأت نفس النائم في السماء فهي الرؤيا الصادقة وما رأت بعد الإرسال فيلقنها الشيطان فهي كاذبة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p56#3/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p56#3/r9.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
NASAFI-FULL:v4p56#3/r9.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says living and dead spirits meet in sleep and recognize what God wills; God holds those decreed dead and sends the others back to their bodies for their remaining lifetimes.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p56#3/r9.anchor: وعن سعيد بن جبير أن أرواح الأحياء وأرواح الأموات تلتقي

NASAFI-FULL:v4p56#3/r10.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p56#3/r10.speaker: رُوي
NASAFI-FULL:v4p56#3/r10.claim: A report says believers' spirits ascend to heaven in sleep; the pure are permitted to prostrate, while the impure are not.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p56#3/r10.anchor: وروى أن أرواح المؤمنين تعرج عند النوم فى السماء فمن كان منهم طاهرا أذن له فى السجود

NASAFI-FULL:v4p56#3/r11.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p56#3/r11.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p56#3/r11.claim: The taking, retaining, and sending back of selves are signs of God's power and knowledge for people who reflect.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p56#3/r11.anchor: إن فى توفى الأنفس مائتة ونائمة وإمساكها وإرسالها إلى أجل ﴿ لآيات ﴾ على قدرة الله وعلمه

QURTUBI-FULL:39:42/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42/r1.claim: God takes souls when their terms end; as for those not dead, He takes them during sleep.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42/r1.anchor: أي يقبضها عند فناء آجالها { والتي لم تمت في منامها

QURTUBI-FULL:39:42/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42/r2.speaker: ابن عيسى
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42/r2.claim: Ibn Isa says sleep seizes a person from activity while the soul remains in the body; God holds the dead and returns the sleeper to activity until death’s term.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42/r2.anchor: فقيل: يقبضها عن التصرف مع بقاء أرواحها في أجسادها

QURTUBI-FULL:39:42/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42/r3.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42/r3.claim: Al-Farra reads the phrase as God taking the sleeper when the appointed term ends; alternatively, sleep itself is called that person’s death.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42/r3.anchor: وقال الفراء: المعنى ويقبض التي لم تمت في منامها عند انقضاء أجلها

QURTUBI-FULL:39:42/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas and other exegetes say living and dead souls meet and recognize one another in sleep; God holds the dead souls and sends living souls back to their bodies.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وغيره من المفسرين: إن أرواح الأحياء والأموات تلتقي في المنام

QURTUBI-FULL:39:42/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42/r5.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says God takes the dead at death and the living in sleep; the souls encounter one another, then the dead are held and the others restored.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42/r5.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: إن الله يقبض أرواح الأموات إذا ماتوا، وأرواح الأحياء إذا ناموا

QURTUBI-FULL:39:42/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42/r6.speaker: علي
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42/r6.claim: Ali says dreams seen while the sleeper’s soul is in heaven before being sent back are true; after dispatch but before settling in the body, devils show it false visions.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42/r6.anchor: قال علي رضي الله عنه: فما رأته نفس النائم وهي في السماء قبل إرسالها إلى جسدها

QURTUBI-FULL:39:42/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd says sleep is a death and death is a death.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42/r7.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: النوم وفاة والموت وفاة

QURTUBI-FULL:39:42/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42/r8.claim: A Prophetic report says people die as they sleep and are resurrected as they wake.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42/r8.anchor: كما تنامون فكذلك تموتون وكما توقظون فكذلك تبعثون

QURTUBI-FULL:39:42/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42/r9.speaker: عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42/r9.claim: Umar calls sleep the sibling of death.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:42/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42/r10.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42/r10.claim: Al-Daraqutni transmits a report from Jabir that the Prophet said the people of Paradise do not sleep, because sleep is death’s sibling and Paradise contains no death.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42/r10.anchor: من حديث جابر بن عبد الله

QURTUBI-FULL:39:42/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas distinguishes a cognitive nafs from a moving, breathing rūḥ; in sleep God takes the nafs but not the rūḥ, a view also attributed to Ibn al-Anbari and al-Zajjaj.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42/r11.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: في ابن آدم نفس وروح بينهما مثل شعاع الشمس

QURTUBI-FULL:39:42/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42/r12.speaker: القشيري أبو نصر
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42/r12.claim: Al-Qushayri objects that the Ibn Abbas distinction is unlikely because the verse’s apparent sense is that the same thing is taken in sleep and death.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42/r12.anchor: قال القشيري أبو نصر: وفي هذا بعد إذ المفهوم من الآية أن النفس المقبوضة في الحالين شيء واحد

QURTUBI-FULL:39:42/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42/r13.claim: God takes the same soul in sleep and death: in sleep He envelops it with restraint that stops activity; in death He holds it until Resurrection.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42/r13.anchor: في حالة النوم وحالة الموت، فما قبضه في حال النوم فمعناه أنه يغمره بما يحبسه

QURTUBI-FULL:39:42/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42/r14.claim: Sending the sleeper’s soul removes its restraint so sensation returns; sleep’s taking removes sensation and creates heedlessness, while death removes sensation completely.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42/r14.anchor: وقوله: { ويرسل الأخرى } أي يزيل الحابس عنه فيعود كما كان.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:42#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42#2/r1.claim: People differed on whether soul and spirit are one or two; al-Qurtubi holds they are one, supported by sound reports cited here.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42#2/r1.anchor: والأظهر أنهما شيء واحد، وهو الذي تدل عليه الآثار الصحاح

QURTUBI-FULL:39:42#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42#2/r2.speaker: أم سلمة
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42#2/r2.claim: Umm Salama reports that the Prophet closed Abu Salama’s eyes when his gaze fixed at death, explaining that sight follows the spirit when it is taken; Muslim records it.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42#2/r2.anchor: حديث أم سلمة قالت: دخل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على أبي سلمة وقد شق بصره فأغمضه، ثم قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:39:42#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42#2/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42#2/r3.claim: Abu Hurayra transmits the Prophet’s explanation that a dying person’s fixed gaze occurs because his sight follows his soul; Muslim records the report.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42#2/r3.anchor: وحديث أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

QURTUBI-FULL:39:42#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42#2/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42#2/r4.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that angels greet the righteous soul as it leaves its good body, promise it good news, and accompany it upward; Ibn Mājah records it with a sound chain.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42#2/r4.anchor: وعنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:39:42#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42#2/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42#2/r5.claim: Abu Hurayra reports in Muslim that when a believer’s spirit leaves, two angels meet it and ascend with it.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42#2/r5.anchor: وفي صحيح مسلم عن أبي هريرة قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:39:42#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42#2/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42#2/r6.claim: In the valley sleep report, Bilal says the one who took his soul also took the Prophet’s; the Prophet says God took their spirits and could have returned them at another time.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42#2/r6.anchor: وقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مقابلا له في حديث زيد بن أسلم في حديث الوادي:

QURTUBI-FULL:39:42#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42#2/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42#2/r7.claim: The soul is a subtle body interwoven with perceptible bodies: it is drawn out, wrapped and carried to heaven, does not die or perish, has a beginning but no end, has eyes and hands, and may smell good or foul; these are bodily, not accidental, properties.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42#2/r7.anchor: والصحيح فيه أنه جسم لطيف مشابك للأجسام المحسوسة، يجذب ويخرج وفي أكفانه يلف ويدرج

QURTUBI-FULL:39:42#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42#2/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42#2/r8.claim: The soul’s departure through the throat is a bodily process, as the verse about the soul reaching the throat describes its exit from the body.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42#2/r8.anchor: وقال تعالى: فلولا إذا بلغت الحلقوم [الواقعة: 83] يعني النفس إلى خروجها من الجسد وهذه صفة الجسم

QURTUBI-FULL:39:42#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42#3/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42#3/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra transmits the Prophet’s bedtime instruction: dust the bed, invoke God, lie on the right side, and ask forgiveness if the soul is retained or protection if it is sent back; Bukhari and Muslim narrate it, with Ibn Mājah and al-Tirmidhī giving a wording variant.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42#3/r1.anchor: إذا أوى أحدكم إلى فراشه فليأخذ داخلة إزاره

QURTUBI-FULL:39:42#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42#3/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42#3/r2.claim: Ibn Mājah, al-Tirmidhī and Bukhari give “have mercy on it” in place of “forgive it”; al-Tirmidhī adds a waking prayer thanking God for restoring the soul and permitting remembrance.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:42#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42#3/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42#3/r3.claim: Hudhayfa reports that the Prophet, when retiring at night, said “In Your name I die and live,” and on waking praised God for reviving them after death and recalled the Resurrection; Bukhari records it.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42#3/r3.anchor: وخرج البخاري عن حذيفة قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:39:42#4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42#4/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42#4/r1.claim: The general reading has active qaḍā and accusative al-mawt, meaning God decreed death; Abu Ḥātim and Abū ʿUbayd chose it. Al-Qurṭubī finds it clearer and better matched to God as subject above and the agreed active reading yursilu.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42#4/r1.anchor: هذه قراءة العامة على أنه مسمى الفاعل { الموت } نصبا أي قضى الله عليها وهو اختيار أبي حاتم وأبي عبيد

QURTUBI-FULL:39:42#4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42#4/r2.speaker: الأعمش ويحيى بن وثاب وحمزة والكسائي
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42#4/r2.claim: Al-Aʿmash, Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read the phrase passively, “death was decreed upon it”; al-Naḥḥās says the meaning is the same.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42#4/r2.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش ويحيى بن وثاب وحمزة والكسائي { قضي عليها الموت } على ما لم يسم فاعله.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:42#4/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42#4/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42#4/r3.claim: The verse demonstrates God’s immense power and exclusive divinity: He acts as He wills, gives life and death, and no one else can do so.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42#4/r3.anchor: وفي الآية تنبيه على عظيم قدرته وانفراده بالألوهية، وأنه يفعل ما يشاء، ويحيي ويميت،

QURTUBI-FULL:39:42#4/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42#4/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42#4/r4.claim: The signs are God’s taking the dead and sleeping souls, sending the sleeper’s soul back and withholding the dead person’s soul.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42#4/r4.anchor: يعني في قبض الله نفس الميت والنائم، وإرساله نفس النائم وحبسه نفس الميت

QURTUBI-FULL:39:42#4/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42#4/r5.speaker: معتمر
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42#4/r5.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī heard Muʿtamir liken the human spirit to a skein of wool: some extends and returns while most remains secretly connected to the body; waking draws the extended portion back.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42#4/r5.anchor: وقال الأصمعي سمعت معتمرا يقول: روح الإنسان مثل كبة الغزل، فترسل الروح، فتمضي ثم تمضي ثم تطوى

QURTUBI-FULL:39:42#4/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42#4/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42#4/r6.claim: The Qur’an says the spirit is from the command of the Lord, so only God knows its true nature; al-Qurṭubī notes that this was discussed earlier in Sūrat al-Isrāʾ.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:42#4/r6.anchor: وفي التنزيل: ويسألونك عن الروح قل الروح من أمر ربي [الإسراء: 85] أي لا يعلم حقيقته إلا الله.

RAZI-FULL:v26p247/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p247/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p247/r1.claim: God retains the soul whose death is decreed, while the soul taken in sleep returns to its body upon waking until its appointed death.
RAZI-FULL:v26p247/r1.anchor: المقصود من الآية أنه تعالى يتوفى الأنفس عند الموت وعند النوم إلا أنه يمسك الأنفس التي قضى عليها الموت ويرسل الأخرى

RAZI-FULL:v26p247/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p247/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p247/r2.claim: The human soul is a luminous spiritual substance: waking illuminates the whole body, sleep withdraws its light partly from the exterior, and death withdraws it entirely.
RAZI-FULL:v26p247/r2.anchor: النفس الإنسانية عبارة عن جوهر مشرق روحاني إذا تعلق بالبدن حصل ضوؤه في جميع الأعضاء وهو الحياة

RAZI-FULL:v26p247/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p247/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p247/r3.claim: The different, carefully ordered relations between soul and body at waking, sleep, and death demonstrate a powerful, knowing, wise Creator; they also call people to worship God rather than inert idols.
RAZI-FULL:v26p247/r3.anchor: ومثل هذا التدبير العجيب لا يمكن صدوره إلا عن القادر العليم الحكيم

RAZI-FULL:v26p247/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p247/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p247/r7.claim: God is the true agent of taking souls, while He delegates this work among created causes to the Angel of Death as chief and other angels as assistants.

STUDYQURAN:39:42/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:42/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:39:42/r1.claim: God takes souls by sending the Angel of Death, as stated in 32:11.
STUDYQURAN:39:42/r1.anchor: God takes souls by sending the Angel of Death to them, as in 32:11

STUDYQURAN:39:42/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:42/r2.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:39:42/r2.claim: R says souls are completely separated from the body in death and partially separated in sleep.
STUDYQURAN:39:42/r2.anchor: In death souls are completely detached from the body, and in sleep they are partially detached (R)

STUDYQURAN:39:42/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:42/r3.speaker: aḥādīth
STUDYQURAN:39:42/r3.claim: Aḥādīth call sleep the brother of death and say the people of the Garden do not die.
STUDYQURAN:39:42/r3.anchor: Sleep is the brother of death, and the people of the Garden do not die” (Q)

STUDYQURAN:39:42/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:42/r4.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:39:42/r4.claim: The Prophet taught a bedtime prayer asking God to show mercy if He takes the sleeper’s soul and to protect it if He returns it.
STUDYQURAN:39:42/r4.anchor: the Prophet advised his Companions to say when going to bed

STUDYQURAN:39:42/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:42/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:39:42/r5.claim: The appointed term can mean death or the Day of Judgment, when all things return to God.
STUDYQURAN:39:42/r5.anchor: A term appointed indicates the moment of death or the Day of Judgment, when all things are returned to God.

STUDYQURAN:39:42/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:42/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:39:42/r6.claim: Every human being and all creation have a decreed term.
STUDYQURAN:39:42/r6.anchor: For all human beings, as for all creation, this term is decreed, as in 6:2

STUDYQURAN:39:42/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:42/r7.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:39:42/r7.claim: R takes the appointed term here as the waking return of souls to bodies, granting reprieve until death and reckoning.
STUDYQURAN:39:42/r7.anchor: till a term appointed refers to the return of souls to their bodies when they awaken (R)

TAB-FULL:v20p215/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p215/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p215/r1.claim: God alone is divine because He alone gives death and life and does what He wills; nothing else has this power.
TAB-FULL:v20p215/r1.anchor: يميت ويحيي، ويفعل ما يشاء، ولا يقدر على ذلك شيء سواه

TAB-FULL:v20p215/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p215/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p215/r2.claim: God takes souls at death and also in sleep; the souls of living and dead meet, then He retains the dead and returns the living to their bodies for the rest of their appointed lives.
TAB-FULL:v20p215/r2.anchor: ذكر أن أرواح الأحياء والأموات تلتقي في المنام، فيتعارف ما شاء الله منها، فإذا أراد جميعها الرجوع إلى أجسادها

TAB-FULL:v20p215/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p215/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v20p215/r3.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says the souls of living and dead meet and recognize as God wills; the dead are retained while the others return to their bodies.
TAB-FULL:v20p215/r3.anchor: سعيد بن جبير، في قوله: {الله يتوفى الأنفس حين موتها} [الزمر: 42] الآية، قال: «يجمع بين أرواح الأحياء، وأرواح الأموات

TAB-FULL:v20p215/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p215/r4.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v20p215/r4.claim: Al-Suddī describes sleep as a taking of souls: they meet and converse; living souls return, while souls decreed to die are held and the rest return for their remaining lifespan.
TAB-FULL:v20p215/r4.anchor: السدي، في قوله: {الله يتوفى الأنفس حين موتها} [الزمر: 42] قال: " تقبض الأرواح عند نيام النائم، فتقبض روحه في منامه

TAB-FULL:v20p215/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p215/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v20p215/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd says sleep is a kind of death; God retains the soul subject to death and sends back the one not seized until its appointed term.
TAB-FULL:v20p215/r5.anchor: ابن زيد، في قوله: {الله يتوفى الأنفس حين موتها والتي لم تمت في منامها} [الزمر: 42] قال: «فالنوم وفاة»

SULAMI:v2p199#4/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p199#4/r1.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v2p199#4/r1.claim: Sahl distinguishes the subtle soul of bodily nature from the subtle spirit: sleep takes the former, while losing the latter ends bodily movement and is death.
SULAMI:v2p199#4/r1.anchor: قال سهل : إن الله إذا توفى الأنفس اخرج الروح النورى من لطيف نفس الطبع الكثيف فالذي يتوفى في النوم

SULAMI:v2p199#4/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p199#4/r2.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v2p199#4/r2.claim: Natural life is sustained by a subtle light, while the subtle spirit is alive through remembrance of God.
SULAMI:v2p199#4/r2.anchor: وقال حياة النفس الطبيعي بنور لطيف وحياة لطيف نفس الروح بالذكر لله .

SULAMI:v2p199#4/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p199#4/r3.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v2p199#4/r3.claim: The spirit can stand by its own subtle essence without bodily nature, as shown by God's address to all people in the primordial realm through spirit, reason, and subtle knowledge.
SULAMI:v2p199#4/r3.anchor: وقال أيضا : الروح تقوم بلطيفة في ذاتها بغير نفس الطبع ألا ترى أن الله خاطب الكل في الذر بنفس روح وفهم عقل

TUSTARI:39:42/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:39:42/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:39:42/r1.claim: Tawaffī in the Qur'an has three senses: death, sleep, and being raised; at death God separates the luminous spirit's subtle self from the dense natural self that enables cognition and visions of the unseen.
TUSTARI:39:42/r1.anchor: والتوفي في كتاب الله على ثلاثة أوجه: أحدها الموت، والآخر النوم

TUSTARI:39:42/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:39:42/r2.speaker: author
TUSTARI:39:42/r2.claim: In sleep, God withdraws the subtle self of dense nature but not the luminous spirit; the sleeper can awaken because that spirit remains, while its departure leaves a being without movement, dead.
TUSTARI:39:42/r2.anchor: وإذا نام نزع عنه لطيف نفس الطبع الكثيف لا لطيف نفس الروح النوري

TUSTARI:39:42/r3.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:39:42/r3.speaker: author
TUSTARI:39:42/r3.claim: The subtle natural self lives by the light of the spirit, while the spirit's own life is remembrance; the dead are called alive with their Lord because they are given remembrance through the luminous spirit.
TUSTARI:39:42/r3.anchor: فحياة لطيف نفس الطبع بنور لطيف نفس الروح، وحياة روح لطيف نفس الروح بالذكر

TUSTARI:39:42/r4.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:39:42/r4.speaker: author
TUSTARI:39:42/r4.claim: Dense nature lives through food, drink, and pleasure; a true knower reconciles nature and spirit so that both live by remembrance and striving in it.
TUSTARI:39:42/r4.anchor: وحياة الطبع الكثيف بالأكل والشرب والتمتع، فمن لم يحسن الإصلاح بين هذين الضدين

TUSTARI:39:42/r5.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:39:42/r5.speaker: المبرد النحوي
TUSTARI:39:42/r5.claim: Al-Mubarrad the grammarian says spirit and soul are two connected things, neither of which can subsist without the other.
TUSTARI:39:42/r5.anchor: وقال عمر بن واصل: وكان المبرد النحوي يقول: الروح والنفس شيئان متصلان

TUSTARI:39:42/r6.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:39:42/r6.speaker: سهل
TUSTARI:39:42/r6.claim: Sahl rejects al-Mubarrad: spirit subsists in its own subtlety without dense nature, as God addressed the primordial beings with spirit, understanding, heart-perception, and subtle knowledge before bodily nature existed.
TUSTARI:39:42/r6.anchor: فذكرت ذلك لسهل، فقال: أخطأ، إن الروح يقوم بلطفه في ذاته بغير نفس الطبع الكثيف

TABATABAI:39:42-43/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:42-43/r1.speaker: المجمع
TABATABAI:39:42-43/r1.claim: Al-Majmaʿ explains tawaffī as taking something fully and completely, as in receiving one’s due in full.
TABATABAI:39:42-43/r1.anchor: قال في المجمع التوفي قبض الشيء على الإيفاء والإتمام يقال توفيت حقي من فلان واستوفيته

TABATABAI:39:42-43/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:42-43/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:42-43/r2.claim: Fronting Allah restricts the true taking of souls to Him; the Angel of Death and assisting angels are intermediate causes acting by His command.
TABATABAI:39:42-43/r2.anchor: تقديم المسند إليه في الآية يفيد الحصر أي هو تعالى المتوفي لها لا غير

TABATABAI:39:42-43/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:42-43/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:42-43/r3.claim: The souls are spirits attached to bodies, not all spirits collectively; death takes the spirit by severing its governing connection to the body, and denotes bodily death here by ellipsis or figurative attribution.
TABATABAI:39:42-43/r3.anchor: المراد بالأنفس الأرواح المتعلقة بالأبدان لا مجموع الأرواح لأن المجموع غير مقبوض عند الموت

TABATABAI:39:42-43/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:42-43/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:42-43/r4.claim: The clause about those who have not died coordinates with souls; al-manām is a time noun, and the phrase means taking souls during their sleep.
TABATABAI:39:42-43/r4.anchor: معطوف على الأنفس في الجملة السابقة، والظاهر أن المنام اسم زمان

TABATABAI:39:42-43/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:42-43/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:42-43/r5.claim: God keeps the sleeping soul whose death He has decreed and does not return it, but returns the other to its body; sending may happen once or repeatedly until its appointed term.
TABATABAI:39:42-43/r5.anchor: ويرسل النفس الأخرى التي لم يقض عليها الموت إلى بدنها إلى أجل مسمى تنتهي إليه الحياة

TABATABAI:39:42-43/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:42-43/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:42-43/r6.claim: The verse shows that the soul exists distinctly from the body, can separate from it, and remains independently.
TABATABAI:39:42-43/r6.anchor: أن النفس موجود مغاير للبدن بحيث تفارقه وتستقل عنه وتبقى بحيالها

TABATABAI:39:42-43/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:42-43/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:42-43/r7.claim: Death and sleep are both forms of taking, but death is not followed by return whereas sleep may be followed by return.
TABATABAI:39:42-43/r7.anchor: أن الموت والنوم كلاهما توف وإن افترقا في أن الموت توف لا إرسال بعده والنوم توف ربما كان بعده إرسال

TABATABAI:39:42-43/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:42-43/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:42-43/r8.claim: Reflection reminds people that God manages their affairs and that they will return to Him to be reckoned for their deeds.
TABATABAI:39:42-43/r8.anchor: فيتذكرون أن الله سبحانه هو المدبر لأمرهم وأنهم إليه راجعون سيحاسبهم على ما عملوا

TABRISI:39:42/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:42/r1.speaker: أهل الكوفة غير عاصم وقتيبة؛ والباقون
TABRISI:39:42/r1.claim: Kufans except ʿĀṣim and Qutayba read passive quḍiya with al-mawt nominative; others read active qaḍā with al-mawt accusative.
TABRISI:39:42/r1.anchor: قرأ أهل الكوفة غير عاصم وقتيبة قضي بالضم الموت بالرفع والباقون قضى بالفتح الموت بالنصب

TABRISI:39:42/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:42/r2.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:39:42/r2.claim: Abū ʿAlī prefers the active reading because it matches active ‘and He sends’; passive has the same sense.
TABRISI:39:42/r2.anchor: قال أبو علي: حجة من بنى الفعل للفاعل قوله { ويرسل الأخرى } فكما أن هذا مبني للفاعل

TABRISI:39:42/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:42/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:42/r3.claim: Tawaffī is taking something fully, as when collecting a debt in full.
TABRISI:39:42/r3.anchor: التوفي قبض الشيء على الإيفاء والإتمام. يقال: توفيت حقي من فلان واستوفيته

TABRISI:39:42/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:42/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:42/r12.claim: God takes souls when bodies die; ‘bodies’ is understood by ellipsis.
TABRISI:39:42/r12.anchor: أي يقبضها إليه وقت موتها وانقضاء آجالها والمعنى حين موت أبدانها وأجسادها على حذف المضاف

TABRISI:39:42/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:42/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:42/r13.claim: Sleep takes the soul of intellect and discernment, leaving the sleeper unable to understand; the life-bearing spirit stays in the body.
TABRISI:39:42/r13.anchor: والتي تتوفى عند النوم هي النفس التي يكون بها العقل والتمييز وهي التي تفارق النائم فلا يعقل

TABRISI:39:42/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:42/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:42/r14.claim: Sleep seizure opposes wakefulness while spirit remains; death seizure opposes life and removes it. God retains the dead until Resurrection and returns sleepers until appointed death.
TABRISI:39:42/r14.anchor: وقبض النوم يكون الروح معه في البدن وقبض الموت يخرج الروح معه من البدن

TABRISI:39:42/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:42/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:42/r15.claim: The alternating seizure of souls in sleep and death proves God’s unity and power; only He can do this.
TABRISI:39:42/r15.anchor: أي دلالات واضحات على توحيد الله وكمال قدرته

TABRISI:39:42-45/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:42-45/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:39:42-45/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās distinguishes soul and spirit in each person like a sunbeam: the soul enables reason and discernment, spirit breathing and movement; sleep seizes soul, death both.
TABRISI:39:42-45/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: في بني آدم نفس وروح بينهما مثل شعاع الشمس فالنفس التي بها العقل والتمييز

TABRISI:39:42-45/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:42-45/r2.speaker: أبو جعفر
TABRISI:39:42-45/r2.claim: Abū Jaʿfar reports a sleeper’s soul ascends to heaven while the spirit remains in the body, linked like a sunbeam; by God’s permission soul and spirit answer each other when taking or return. Heavenly visions have interpretation; visions between heaven and earth are Satan’s illusion without interpretation.
TABRISI:39:42-45/r2.anchor: عن أبي جعفر ع قال: ما من أحد ينام إلا عرجت نفسه إلى السماء وبقيت روحه في بدنه وصار بينهما سبب كشعاع الشمس

TABRISI:39:42-45/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:42-45/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:42-45/r10.claim: This connects with the Prophet not being their guardian: God keeps them, takes them, and directs them as He wills.
TABRISI:39:42-45/r10.anchor: اتصل قوله { الله يتوفى الأنفس } بقوله { وما أنت عليهم بوكيل } فبين سبحانه أن الحفيظ عليهم هو الذي يتوفاهم

TABRISI:39:42-45/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:42-45/r11.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:39:42-45/r11.claim: Another connection is to 39:36, ‘Is God not sufficient for His servant?’; one with this power is sufficient for the Prophet.
TABRISI:39:42-45/r11.anchor: وقيل: يتصل بقوله { أليس الله بكاف عبده } أي من كان هذه صفته فإنه يكفيك أمرهم

THALABI:v8p238/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p238/r1.speaker: أبو عبيد وأبو حاتم
THALABI:v8p238/r1.claim: Abu Ubayd and Abu Hatim prefer the remaining readers' fatḥ reading, reasoning from God's taking souls at death: He decrees death upon them.
THALABI:v8p238/r1.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بفتحها، واختاره أبو عبيد وأبو حاتم، قالا: لقوله (الله يتوفى الأنفس حين موتها) فهو يقضي عليها.

THALABI:v8p238/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p238/r2.speaker: المفسرون
THALABI:v8p238/r2.claim: Commentators say living and dead souls meet and recognize one another in sleep; God holds the dead souls and sends the living back to their bodies.
THALABI:v8p238/r2.anchor: قال المفسرون: إن أرواح الأحياء والأموات تلتقي في المنام فيتعارف ما شاء الله تعالى منها، فإذا أراد جميعها الرجوع إلى أجسادها،

THALABI:v8p238/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p238/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p238/r3.claim: The appointed term is the end of the person's lifespan.
THALABI:v8p238/r3.anchor: إلى أجل مسمى وقت انقضاء مدة حياتها إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يتفكرون.

THALABI:v8p238/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p238/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
THALABI:v8p238/r4.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says God takes the souls of both living and dead, holds those of the dead, and sends the living back until their appointed term, without error.
THALABI:v8p238/r4.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير في قوله تعالى: الله يتوفى الأنفس حين موتها قال: يقبض أنفس الأموات والأحياء، فيمسك أنفس الأموات ويرسل أنفس الأحياء إلى أجل مسمى لا يغلط.

THALABI:v8p238/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p238/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v8p238/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas distinguishes the nafs, which provides intellect and discernment, from the ruh, which provides breath and movement; in sleep God takes the nafs but not the ruh.
THALABI:v8p238/r5.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: في ابن آدم نفس وروح بينهما مثل شعاع الشمس، فالنفس التي بها العقل والتمييز، والروح التي بها النفس والتحرك، فإذا نام العبد قبض الله نفسه ولم يقبض روحه.

THALABI:v8p238/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p238/r6.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v8p238/r6.claim: Abu Hurayra transmits the Prophet's bedtime supplication: lie on the right side, ask forgiveness if God holds one's soul, and protection if He releases it.
THALABI:v8p238/r6.anchor: عن أبي هريرة ان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «إذا أوى أحدكم إلى فراشه، فليضطجع على شقه الأيمن وليقل:

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p24/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p24/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p24/r1.claim: Yatawaffā derives from istīfāʾ, taking something fully; tawaffaytuhu and istawfaytuhu, like other doubled forms, express this. Death was later called wafāt or waf.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p24/r1.anchor: هو من استيفاء العدد واستيفاء الشيء إذا استقصيته كله

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p24/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p24/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p24/r2.claim: Arabs call blood nafs because it is connected to breath, following their practice of naming things for what is associated, adjacent, or causative.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p24/r2.anchor: والعرب تسمى الدم نفسا لاتصال النفس به على مذهبهم في تسمية الشيء بما اتصل به أو جاوره أو كان سببا له

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p24/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p24/r3.speaker: أصحاب اللغة
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p24/r3.claim: The Arabs use nafisat al-marʾa for menstruation, as if she bled; lexicographers explain nafisāʾ as named for the flow of blood.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p24/r3.anchor: ويقولون: نفست المرأة: إذا حاضت كأنها دميت. وقال أصحاب اللغة: وإنما سميت المرأة نفساء لسيلان الدم.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p24/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p24/r4.speaker: إبراهيم
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p24/r4.claim: Ibrahim says anything without flowing blood does not render water impure if it falls into it; here nafs means flowing blood.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p24/r4.anchor: وقال إبراهيم (1) : كل شيء ليست له نفس سائلة فإنه لا ينجس الماء إذا سقط فيه

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p24/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p24/r5.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p24/r5.claim: The Arabs also call the soul nasama, whose root is nafas.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p24/r5.anchor: وتسمى العرب النفس نسمة. وأصل النسمة النفس.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p24/r6.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p24/r6.speaker: بعض الحديث
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p24/r6.claim: An unnamed hadith says to avoid dust because nasama comes from it; Ibn Qutayba explains nasama here as breath.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p24/r6.anchor: وروي في بعض الحديث "تنكبوا الغبار فإن منه تكون النسمة" (2) يراد منه يكون النفس.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p24/r7.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p24/r7.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p24/r7.claim: Rabw is called nafs because it arises from breathing.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p24/r7.anchor: والربو سمي نفسا لأنه عن النفس يكون

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p24/r8.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p24/r8.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p24/r8.claim: The idioms ḥatfa nafsihi and ḥatfa anfihi mean dying in bed: breathing continues until death, when the soul leaves through the nose and mouth.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p24/r8.anchor: والعرب تقول: مات فلان حتف نفسه، وحتف أنفه إذا مات على فراشه؛

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:42-45/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:42-45/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:42-45/r1.claim: God takes souls at death and also takes the souls of those who have not died during sleep; He keeps the dead and returns the others when they wake, until their appointed time of death.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:42-45/r1.anchor: يقْبض الأرواح { حين } عند { موتها والتي لم تمت } أي: ويقبض روح التي لم تمت

MAJAZ:v2p190/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p190/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p190/r1.claim: God takes souls both at death and during sleep, but returns the sleeping soul to the world while retaining the soul whose death He has decreed.
MAJAZ:v2p190/r1.anchor: فجعل النائم متوفى أيضا إلا أنه يرده إلى الدنيا

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:42/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:42/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:42/r1.claim: The preceding verse ties guidance and misguidance to human choice; this verse directs attention to God and the wisdom of creation and governance, before further proofs follow.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:42/r1.anchor: Bir önceki âyette insanların hidayete yönelmelerinin de yoldan çıkmalarının da kendi seçimlerine bağlı bulunduğuna işaret edilmişti.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:42/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:42/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:42/r2.claim: Possession of a soul is the basic distinction between humans and other beings; God’s taking a person in death severs the soul’s relation to the body, and the soul is the source of life and consciousness.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:42/r2.anchor: İnsanı öteki varlıklardan ayıran en temel özelliği ruh sahibi bir varlık oluşudur. Allah Teâlâ’nın insanı öldürmesi, ruhun bedenle ilişkisini kesmesidir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:42/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:42/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:42/r3.claim: At death the soul leaves the body completely, removing life and consciousness; in sleep life remains while sensation and awareness are temporarily lost, so sleep is likened to death as a partial departure of the soul.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:42/r3.anchor: Bu kayıp bir bakıma ruhun bedeni kısmen terketmesi anlamına geldiği için âyette uyku ölüme benzetilmiştir (Zemahşerî, IV, 349).

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:42/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:42/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:42/r4.claim: God holds the soul at death; after sleep it regains waking function, but this too lasts only to an appointed term, and everyone ultimately returns to God.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:42/r4.anchor: Ölüm olayında –âyetteki deyimiyle– Allah ruhu tutarken uyku olayının sonunda ruh, uyanıklıktaki fonksiyonunu yeniden kazanır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:42/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:42/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:42/r5.claim: The relation among nafs, rūḥ, and the human being is also discussed at 4:1 and 17:85.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:42/r5.anchor: nefis-ruh-insan ilişkisi için bk. Nisâ 4/1; İsrâ 17/85

ITQAN:v3p247#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p247#2/r1.speaker: الطيبي
ITQAN:v3p247#2/r1.claim: Al-Tibi calls this الجمع والتفريق: the verse groups souls under God's taking, then distinguishes the two kinds by saying one is held and the other sent back.
ITQAN:v3p247#2/r1.anchor: وجعل منه الطيبي قوله ﴿ الله يتوفى الأنفس حين موتها ﴾ الآية جمع النفسين في حكم المتوفي ثم فرق بين جهتي التوفي بالحكم بالإمساك والإرسال

NAHHAS:v4p13/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p13/r8.speaker: يحيى بن وثاب
NAHHAS:v4p13/r8.claim: Yahya ibn Waththab, al-A'mash, Hamza, and al-Kisa'i read فيمسك passively; the meaning is unchanged, but al-Nahhas prefers the active reading because ويرسل is unanimously active and the sequence is clearer.
NAHHAS:v4p13/r8.anchor: وقراءة يحيى بن وثاب والأعمش وحمزة والكسائي

TABATABAI:39:38-52/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:38-52/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:38-52/r1.claim: The discussion distinguishes true visions of the greater imaginal realm from satanic fantasies arising in the lesser imaginal realm, which have no interpretation.
TABATABAI:39:38-52/r1.anchor: فمهما رأت في ملكوت السماوات فهو مما له تأويل

TABATABAI:39:38-52/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:38-52/r2.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
TABATABAI:39:38-52/r2.claim: ʿAlī explains to ʿUmar that God takes all souls in sleep and death: visions seen while souls are with God in heaven are true, while devils fabricate falsehoods when souls return to their bodies.
TABATABAI:39:38-52/r2.anchor: فقال علي بن أبي طالب أفلا أخبرك بذلك يا أمير المؤمنين

TABATABAI:39:38-52/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:38-52/r3.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
TABATABAI:39:38-52/r3.claim: ʿUmar marvels that some dreams prove exactly true while others amount to nothing; the report is transmitted from Sulaym b. ʿĀmir through Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Ibn Mardawayh.
TABATABAI:39:38-52/r3.anchor: عن سليم بن عامر أن عمر بن الخطاب قال العجب من رؤيا الرجل

TABATABAI:39:38-52/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:38-52/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:38-52/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī directs readers to his fuller treatment of dreams in Sūrat Yūsuf and interprets “heaven” and “between heaven and earth” as the greater and lesser imaginal worlds.
TABATABAI:39:38-52/r4.anchor: أقول تقدم تفصيل الكلام في الرؤيا في سورة يوسف والرجوع إليه

ELMALILI:39:42-52/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:39:42-52/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:39:42-52/r3.claim: The verse looks back to the statement that the Prophet is not their guardian: God is, since He alone takes souls; Elmalılı says this is made explicit later in the sura.
ELMALILI:39:42-52/r3.anchor: Bir kere kasr ile nihâyetteki وَمَآ أَنتَ عَلَيْهِم بِوَكِيلٍ kavline nâzırdır. Yani vekil sen değilsin Allah’tır.

ELMALILI:39:42-52/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:39:42-52/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:39:42-52/r4.claim: Death and sleep provide an analogy for guidance and misguidance.
ELMALILI:39:42-52/r4.anchor: ikincisi hidâyet ve dalâletin, hayat ve memat ile bir temsîlini iş‘âr eder.

ELMALILI:39:42-52/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:39:42-52/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:39:42-52/r5.claim: The verse clarifies the earlier statement that the Prophet and his opponents will die and dispute before their Lord, confirming the reminder in Yunus 10:108 that guidance or error ultimately affects each person himself.
ELMALILI:39:42-52/r5.anchor: tâ yukarıdaki إِنَّكَ مَيِّتٌۭ وَإِنَّهُم مَّيِّتُونَ ثُمَّ إِنَّكُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ عِندَ رَبِّكُمْ تَخْتَصِمُونَ kavlini bir nevi tavzih ile

ELMALILI:39:42-52/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:39:42-52/r6.speaker: Sâhib-i Keşşâf
ELMALILI:39:42-52/r6.claim: Al-Kashshaf takes ‘selves’ as the whole soul-and-body entity; taking them means causing death by removing the conditions that sustain a living, sensing, perceiving being, since intellect alone is not described as dying or sleeping.
ELMALILI:39:42-52/r6.anchor: Sâhib-i Keşşâf burada “enfüs”ten murad rûh ile beden mecmû‘u olduğuna kāil olarak demiştir ki

ELMALILI:39:42-52/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:39:42-52/r7.speaker: diğer müfessirîn
ELMALILI:39:42-52/r7.claim: Other exegetes, citing Ibn Abbas, take ‘selves’ as rational souls and explain taking them as severing their attachment and control over the body, inwardly and outwardly in death but outwardly only in sleep.
ELMALILI:39:42-52/r7.anchor: İbn Abbas Hazretleri’nden vârid olan bir rivayet vechile

ELMALILI:39:42-52/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:39:42-52/r8.speaker: İbn Abbas
ELMALILI:39:42-52/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas distinguishes the reasoning, discerning nafs from the breathing, moving ruh, comparing them to the sun and its rays; both are taken at death, but only the nafs during sleep.
ELMALILI:39:42-52/r8.anchor: İbn Abbas Hazretleri demiştir ki: “Âdem oğlunda bir nefis bir rûh vardır, aralarındaki fark Güneş ile şu‘âı gibidir.

ELMALILI:39:42-52/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:39:42-52/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:39:42-52/r9.claim: Elmalılı says the sun-and-ray comparison does not imply that the nafs and ruh are different substances.
ELMALILI:39:42-52/r9.anchor: Güneş ile şu‘âını temsil getirmesi gösterir ki aralarında bir cevher farkı anlatmak istememiştir

ELMALILI:39:42-52/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:39:42-52/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:39:42-52/r10.claim: He understands the nafs as the self-aware person, conscious of itself and what is within it, with the paired aspects of perceiver and perceived.
ELMALILI:39:42-52/r10.anchor: Bizim anladığımız şudur: Nefis kendini duyan, kendine ve kendindekine vicdânı olan, yani ene şuuruna sâhip olan zattır.

ELMALILI:39:42-52/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:39:42-52/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:39:42-52/r11.claim: Tawaffi means taking something fully and completely; hence the soul’s complete retrieval by God is called tawaffi and death wafat, like fully honoring a trust by delivering it.
ELMALILI:39:42-52/r11.anchor: Teveffî, bir şeyi vâfî olarak, yani kâmilen ve tamamıyla almak, selb etmektir.

ELMALILI:39:42-52/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:39:42-52/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:39:42-52/r12.claim: Souls are not necessary beings: their consciousness is from God rather than inherent in their essence, and God can take them from themselves; Elmalılı compares this to 8:24.

ELMALILI:39:42-52/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:39:42-52/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:39:42-52/r13.claim: God takes rational selves without destroying them, removing awareness and discernment: at death bodily attachment ceases and the soul is retained; in sleep, souls not destined to die are released until their appointed term.
ELMALILI:39:42-52/r13.anchor: İşte nefsin teveffîsi, ölüm ve uyku hâllerinde olduğu gibi kendinden geçirilip akl u temyîzinin kendinden alınmasıdır.

ELMALILI:39:42-52/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:39:42-52/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:39:42-52/r14.claim: Elmalılı raises how this verse’s attribution of taking souls to God relates to the earlier statements that the Angel of Death and God’s envoys take them; the excerpt ends before his answer.
ELMALILI:39:42-52/r14.anchor: ٱلْمَوْتُ تَوَفَّتْهُ رُسُلُنَا وَهُمْ لَا يُفَرِّطُونَ

ELMALILI:39:42-52#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:39:42-52#2/r1.speaker: Fahreddin Râzî
ELMALILI:39:42-52#2/r1.claim: Râzî says God alone truly takes souls, while angels perform delegated tasks; other verses attribute the taking to angels by agency, while this one attributes it to God in reality.
ELMALILI:39:42-52#2/r1.anchor: Fahreddin Râzî tefsirinde buna şöyle bir cevap verilmiştir: “Hakikatte teveffî eden ancak Allah teâlâ’dır.

ELMALILI:39:42-52#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:39:42-52#2/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:39:42-52#2/r2.claim: Elmalılı accepts Râzî’s account but stresses that this verse describes the instant of return to God, a more important nuance than the general attribution of death to God through angels.
ELMALILI:39:42-52#2/r2.anchor: Buradaki teveffî o ircâ‘ve red lahzasını beyandır.

ELMALILI:39:42-52#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:39:42-52#2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:39:42-52#2/r3.claim: The Angel of Death takes the bodily life called the animal soul, whereas God directly takes the rational soul, the human spirit breathed by the Lord.

ELMALILI:39:42-52#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:39:42-52#2/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:39:42-52#2/r4.claim: The verses saying people are returned to God after death indicate that the rational soul’s taking is uniquely and directly God’s act.
ELMALILI:39:42-52#2/r4.anchor: ثُمَّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكُمْ تُرْجَعُونَ [es-Secde 32/11] buyurulması da bu ihtisâsı iş‘âr eyler.

ELMALILI:39:42-52#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:39:42-52#2/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:39:42-52#2/r5.claim: Taking, withholding, and releasing souls point to God’s sole divinity, final return, resurrection and judgment, and the contrasting fates of disbelievers and the faithful; he links this to the declaration that we belong to God and return to Him.
ELMALILI:39:42-52#2/r5.anchor: إِنَّا لِلَّهِ وَإِنَّآ إِلَيْهِ رَٰجِعُونَ [el-Bakara 2/156] mısdâkına delâlet ederler

ELMALILI:39:42-52#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:39:42-52#2/r6.speaker: Sâhib-i Keşşâf
ELMALILI:39:42-52#2/r6.claim: To answer whether sleep-like separation of the soul would spare disbelievers the experience of punishment, the author reports al-Kashshāf’s view that the rational soul is not subject to death.
ELMALILI:39:42-52#2/r6.anchor: Sâhib-i Keşşâf bu suâle meydan vermemek için

ELMALILI:39:42-52#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:39:42-52#2/r7.speaker: Hazret-i Ali
ELMALILI:39:42-52#2/r7.claim: Elmalılı gives as the real answer a couplet attributed to Ali: if the dead were simply left, death would be rest, but they are resurrected and questioned about everything.
ELMALILI:39:42-52#2/r7.anchor: asıl cevâbı Hazret-i Ali’ye nisbet olunan şu kıtadadır

ELMALILI:39:42-52#2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:39:42-52#2/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:39:42-52#2/r8.claim: God’s absolute control over taking, retaining, and releasing souls shows that this restraint is a detention for resurrection, not an escape; one should reflect on the awe, majesty, and beauty of meeting God.
ELMALILI:39:42-52#2/r8.anchor: bu habs ü imsâkin onları kaçırmayıp ba‘s için bir habs ü tevkif olduğunu istintac etmek

ELMALILI:39:42-52#2/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:39:42-52#2/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:39:42-52#2/r9.claim: At the trumpet blast, disbelievers will ask who raised them from their resting place, which clarifies this point about detention for resurrection.
ELMALILI:39:42-52#2/r9.anchor: Yâsîn’de geçtiği üzere Sûr nefh olununca kâfirler

ELMALILI:39:42-52#2/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:39:42-52#2/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:39:42-52#2/r10.claim: For the same reason, disbelievers will say that God caused them to die twice and live twice.
ELMALILI:39:42-52#2/r10.anchor: Ve yine bundan dolayıdır ki kâfirler

BURHAN:v3p354/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p354/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p354/r3.claim: Plural forms can serve for either few or many because they share the general sense of plurality; one explanation says the generic article makes al-ghurufat comprehensive while signaling that only few believers dwell there.
BURHAN:v3p354/r3.anchor: لأن الجموع يقع بعضها موقع بعض لاشتراكها في مطلق الجمعية

BURHAN:v2p64/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p64/r1.speaker: البغوي
BURHAN:v2p64/r1.claim: Al-Baghawi reconciles the verses: angels seize and extract souls, the Angel of Death summons them and orders his assistants to take them, and God creates death in them.
BURHAN:v2p64/r1.anchor: وجمع البغوي بينها لأن توفي الملائكة بالقبض والنزع وتوفي ملك الموت بالدعاء والأمر

FARRA:v2p419/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p419/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p419/r4.claim: One account says God takes the living in sleep when their appointed term ends; another says their being taken is sleep itself. Al-Farrāʾ prefers the latter.
FARRA:v2p419/r4.anchor: ويقال: إن توفيها نومها. وهو أحب الوجهين إلي لقوله (فيمسك التي قضى عليها الموت)

FARRA:v2p419/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p419/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p419/r5.claim: Both qaḍā ʿalayhā al-mawt and quḍiya ʿalayhā al-mawt are read.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#2/r8.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#2/r8.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#2/r8.claim: Al-Zumar's use of 'struck down' coheres with its references to death and God's taking of souls in sleep and death.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#2/r8.anchor: وكيف ناسب ذكر الصعقة في الزمر قوله تعالى:

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p557/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p557/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p557/r2.claim: The word yatawaffā is elided after allātī lam tamut; the author supplies it in his translation.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p557/r2.anchor: The word  اَاهَّفَوَتَی is suppressed after  يِتَّالَو ْمَل ْتُمَت

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p557/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p557/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p557/r3.claim: God controls life and death: He takes souls whose term is complete, while sleep and waking daily enact death and return to life for those whose term remains; life lasts only for its appointed period.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p557/r3.anchor: When a person sleeps everyday, it is as if he is made to observe death

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p557/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p557/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p557/r4.claim: The first sign is that God’s control over creation, authority, life, and death means no one else has a say in where people return.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p557/r4.anchor: when no one has any say in life and death how can someone become the person to whom people return?

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p558/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p558/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p558/r1.claim: From the first sign Islahi concludes that God alone is worthy of trust, and the trusting should rely on Him.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p558/r1.anchor: trusted; it is on Him those who trust should trust.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p558/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p558/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p558/r2.claim: The second sign is that resurrection is not improbable: daily sleep and waking rehearse death and renewed life, as the believer’s morning supplication reflects.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p558/r2.anchor: a person witnesses a rehearsal of life and death everyday if only he is a man of vision.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p558/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p558/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p558/r3.claim: The third sign is that the universe educates people in Qur’anic truths on which their success and salvation depend.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p558/r3.anchor: the best place for the education of facts on which rests a person’s success and salvation

NASHR:v2p362#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p362#2/r8.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p362#2/r8.claim: Hamza, al-Kisaʾi, and Khalaf read قضي passively and put الموت in the nominative; the others read قضى actively and put الموت in the accusative.
NASHR:v2p362#2/r8.anchor: فقرأ حمزة والكسائي وخلف، قضي بضم القاف

DURR-FULL:v7p229/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p229/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p229/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas distinguishes soul and spirit: God takes the soul during sleep while the spirit remains in the body; if He decrees death He takes the spirit, otherwise He returns the soul to its place.
DURR-FULL:v7p229/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {الله يتوفى الأنفس} الآية قال: نفس وروح بينهما شعاع الشمس فيتوفى الله النفس

DURR-FULL:v7p229/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p229/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p229/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says the souls of living and dead people meet and converse in sleep; God retains the dead and returns the living to their bodies until their appointed term, without error.
DURR-FULL:v7p229/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {الله يتوفى الأنفس حين موتها} الآية قال: يلتقي أرواح الأحياء وأرواح الأموات في المنام

DURR-FULL:v7p229/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p229/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p229/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says each soul has a course it follows: the one whose death is decreed sleeps until that course is cut off, while the one not dead is left.
DURR-FULL:v7p229/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {الله يتوفى الأنفس حين موتها} قال: كل نفس لها سبب تجري فيه

DURR-FULL:v7p229/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p229/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p229/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas, in a report through Juwaybir, describes a cord stretched between heaven and earth to which living and dead souls attach; God holds the dead soul and sends the living one back to its body.
DURR-FULL:v7p229/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس في الآية قال: سبب ممدود بين السماء والأرض فأرواح الموتى وأرواح الأحياء

DURR-FULL:v7p229/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p229/r9.speaker: فرقد
DURR-FULL:v7p229/r9.claim: Farqad says God takes all souls each night, asks what each person did that day, then orders the Angel of Death to take those decreed to die and sends the others back until their appointed term.
DURR-FULL:v7p229/r9.anchor: عن فرقد قال: ما من ليلة من ليالي الدنيا إلا والرب تبارك وتعالى يقبض الأرواح كلها مؤمنها وكافرها
